kcs.label: Reflexive verbs for daily routine
kcs.description: Many routine verbs are used with a reflexive pronoun matching the subject: me levanto, te duchas, se llama, nos acostamos, os vestís, se lavan. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or is attached to an infinitive (Voy a ducharme).
forms: me, te, se, nos, os, se + verb
levantarse, ducharse, lavarse, vestirse, acostarse, llamarse
attached to infinitive: Tengo que levantarme. (A2)
reflexive vs not: Lavo el coche. / Me lavo.
Latin American tendency to more reflexive use: desayunarse (recognition)

examples.es: Me levanto a las siete y me ducho rápido.
examples.en: I get up at seven and shower quickly.

examples.es: ¿Cómo se llama tu perro?
examples.en: What's your dog called?

mastery: Matches reflexive pronouns with subjects
Describes a morning routine with five reflexive verbs
Distinguishes lavar (something) from lavarse
commonErrors: EN: leaves out the pronoun: *Levanto a las siete
EN: uses the wrong person: *Nos levanto
EN: uses possessive with body parts: *Me lavo mis manos (Me lavo las manos)
boundaries: Stem changes in acostarse, vestirse are kt:es-present-stem-change; pronoun position in general is kt:es-clitic-position
Other uses of se (impersonal, passive) are B1

primitives.binding: Pairs Lava el perro / Se lava; learner chooses which picture each sentence describes
Picture strip of a morning; learner orders it and retells with reflexive verbs and times

kcs.label: Telling the time and times of day
kcs.description: Es la una / Son las dos, tres…; y cuarto, y media, menos cuarto, menos diez. A la(s) gives the time of an event (La clase es a las cinco). Parts of the day: de la mañana, de la tarde, de la noche, al mediodía; written 11.30 or 11:30; timetables use the 24-hour clock.
forms: Es la una. / Son las cuatro.
y cuarto, y media, menos cuarto, menos veinte
de la mañana / de la tarde / de la noche
Latin America also: veinte para las diez

examples.es: ¿Qué hora es? – Son las diez menos cuarto.
examples.en: What time is it? – It's quarter to ten.

examples.es: ¿A qué hora abre el banco? – A las ocho y media.
examples.en: What time does the bank open? – At half past eight.

mastery: Writes times heard in natural speech
Answers ¿Qué hora es? and ¿A qué hora…? correctly with es la / son las / a las
Arranges a meeting time and reads a timetable in 24-hour format
commonErrors: EN: *Es las tres (son with plural hours)
EN: says *las tres y cuarenta y cinco in speech; menos cuarto is the usual everyday form (veinte para las diez is common in much of Latin America)
EN: says a las for "it is": *A las tres. for ¿Qué hora es?
boundaries: Durations (dos horas, desde hace) are kt:es-duration-desde-hace
Daily schedules as a social custom are in kt:es-soc-meals-timing

primitives.binding: Announcements and conversations with times; learner fills a schedule; errors grouped by y/menos, cuarto/media, 12/24-hour
A real bus timetable and shop opening hours; learner finds the time needed to make a plan

kcs.label: Days, months, seasons and dates
kcs.description: Days (lunes … domingo) and months (enero … diciembre) are written in lower case. El lunes = on Monday; los lunes = on Mondays. Dates: el 9 de julio (de 2025); ¿Qué día es hoy? – Hoy es martes. Seasons: la primavera, el verano, el otoño, el invierno; en + month/season.
forms: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo
el lunes (this/next Monday) / los lunes (every Monday)
enero … diciembre; en agosto, en invierno
ayer, hoy, mañana; el fin de semana

examples.es: El examen es el viernes 12 de junio.
examples.en: The exam is on Friday 12 June.

examples.es: Los sábados voy al mercado.
examples.en: On Saturdays I go to the market.

mastery: Writes dates in Spanish order with lower case
Distinguishes el lunes from los lunes in meaning
Says their birthday and plans for the week with days and dates
commonErrors: EN: capitalises days and months: *Lunes, *Enero
EN: *en lunes for "on Monday" (el lunes)
EN: month-first date order: *mayo 3
boundaries: Clock time is kt:es-telling-time; past time markers are kt:es-past-time-markers
Public holidays and festivities are kt:es-fn-celebrations-wishes

primitives.binding: Pairs El lunes voy al gimnasio / Los lunes voy al gimnasio; learner marks once or every week on a calendar
Weekly planner page: learner fills in days and dates; check lower case and day–number–de–month order

kcs.label: Present tense with a future time marker
kcs.description: With a time expression, the present tense talks about plans and arrangements: Mañana trabajo. El domingo voy de excursión. This lets A1 learners talk about the near future before learning ir a + infinitive.
forms: time marker + present: Esta noche hago los deberes.
markers: mañana, esta tarde, esta noche, el sábado, la semana que viene

examples.es: ¿Qué haces el sábado? – Ceno con mis padres.
examples.en: What are you doing on Saturday? – I'm having dinner with my parents.

examples.es: Mañana no tengo clase.
examples.en: Tomorrow I don't have class.

mastery: Recognises future meaning from the time marker
Answers ¿Qué haces + time? with a present-tense plan
Plans a weekend with a partner using days and the present
commonErrors: EN: tries to translate "will": *voluntad or invents a future
EN: omits the time marker so the plan reads as a habit
boundaries: ir a + infinitive is kt:es-ir-a-infinitive; the simple future is recognised in kt:es-future-simple-recognition

primitives.binding: Timeline with today, tomorrow and Saturday; learner places sentences (Mañana trabajo / Trabajo los lunes) as plan or habit
Two diaries with gaps; learners ask ¿Qué haces el…? to find a free evening

kcs.label: Daily routine, sequence and personal care
kcs.description: Verbs and chunks for a typical day: despertarse, levantarse, ducharse, lavarse los dientes, desayunar, ir al trabajo/a clase, comer, volver a casa, cenar, acostarse; sequencing with primero, antes, después, luego; temprano, tarde.

kcs.label: Hay: there is / there are
kcs.description: Hay (from haber) is invariable and means "there is / there are". It introduces something new, so it goes with indefinite articles, numbers, quantifiers or bare nouns: Hay un banco / dos bancos / mucha gente / leche. Not with el/la: *Hay el banco.
forms: hay + number / mucho / bastante / poco + noun
hay + bare plural or mass noun: Hay árboles. No hay leche.

examples.es: En mi barrio hay dos farmacias y un mercado.
examples.en: In my neighbourhood there are two pharmacies and a market.

examples.es: ¿Hay leche en la nevera? – No, no hay.
examples.en: Is there any milk in the fridge? – No, there isn't.

mastery: Chooses hay with indefinite/quantified nouns
Describes a room or town with hay and numbers
Asks ¿Hay… cerca? to find services in a town role play
commonErrors: EN: *Hay el banco en la plaza
EN: *Hayn / *Están dos farmacias (hay never agrees)
EN: translates "there is" with *allí es
boundaries: Contrast with estar is kt:es-hay-vs-estar
Past hubo/había are kt:es-preterite-irregular and kt:es-imperfect

primitives.binding: Room picture: learner lists what there is with hay + quantity; check items exist in the picture and counts are right
Two town maps with different services; learners ask ¿Hay una farmacia cerca? to find differences

kcs.label: Estar for location
kcs.description: Estar (estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están) locates known people and things: El banco está en la plaza. ¿Dónde está Ana? Estar is also used for bien/mal (Estoy bien). Location of events uses ser (La fiesta es en mi casa) – taught later.
forms: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están
known subject + está + place: Las llaves están en la mesa.

examples.es: ¿Dónde está la estación? – Está cerca, a la derecha.
examples.en: Where is the station? – It's nearby, on the right.

examples.es: Mis padres están en Cancún esta semana.
examples.en: My parents are in Cancún this week.

mastery: Conjugates estar in all persons
Says where pictured objects are
Asks for and gives the location of places on a map
commonErrors: EN: uses ser for location: *El banco es en la plaza
EN: no stress on the ending: *ESta for está (stressed estÁ)
boundaries: hay vs estar is kt:es-hay-vs-estar; estar + adjective is kt:es-estar-states
Place prepositions are kt:es-place-expressions

primitives.binding: Hear "Las llaves están debajo del libro" and drag objects to that place on a room picture
estar grid then unseen subjects (tus amigos y tú, el profesor); stressed endings shown

kcs.label: Hay or estar?
kcs.description: Hay introduces something new or says whether something exists (Hay un museo en el centro). Estar locates something already known or specific (El museo está en el centro). Clue: after hay come un, números, mucho or bare nouns; before está/están comes el/la, a name or a possessive.
forms: ¿Hay un banco por aquí? – Sí, hay uno en la esquina.
¿Dónde está el Banco Central? – Está en la calle Mayor.

examples.es: Hay un restaurante muy bueno en mi calle. El restaurante está al lado del cine.
examples.en: There's a very good restaurant in my street. The restaurant is next to the cinema.

examples.es: ¿Dónde están mis gafas? ¿Hay unas gafas en la mesa?
examples.en: Where are my glasses? Are there some glasses on the table?

mastery: Chooses hay or está/están in a mixed gap-fill
Explains the choice using the article clue
Describes a town plan using both correctly
commonErrors: EN: *Hay el museo en el centro
EN: *Un banco está en la plaza (for new information hay is preferred)
boundaries: Location of events with ser (La fiesta es en…) is noted in kt:es-ser-vs-estar

primitives.binding: For each sentence learner decides: introducing a new thing or locating a known one; picks hay or estar and sees how the other choice reads
Only the determiner signals the choice (un/el, dos/los); learner must look at it to choose

kcs.label: Saying where: place adverbs and prepositions
kcs.term: cerca de, al lado de, aquí, allí
kcs.description: Location phrases: aquí, ahí, allí (Latin America also acá, allá); cerca (de), lejos (de), al lado (de), a la derecha/izquierda (de), en el centro (de), entre, en. de + el contracts: al lado del banco. A2 adds encima/debajo, delante/detrás, dentro/fuera, enfrente (de).
forms: al lado de, a la derecha de, a la izquierda de
al final de, en el centro de
A2: encima de, debajo de, delante de, detrás de, enfrente de, dentro de, fuera de

examples.es: La farmacia está entre el banco y la panadería.
examples.en: The pharmacy is between the bank and the bakery.

examples.es: Mi casa está muy lejos del centro.
examples.en: My house is very far from the centre.

mastery: Matches location phrases to pictures
Places objects on a plan following spoken instructions
Describes where five places in their town are
commonErrors: EN: *cerca el banco (de is needed)
EN: *al lado de el (del)
EN: confuses en (in/on/at) with English distinctions and adds *sobre everywhere
boundaries: Giving directions is kt:es-fn-directions-basic
Fine distinctions encima/sobre are beyond A2

primitives.binding: Instructions "Pon el gato al lado de la silla" moved onto a picture; the placement is the evidence
Scene picture: learner links each object to its landmark and chooses the preposition phrase

kcs.label: Home and town
kcs.description: Rooms and furniture (la cocina, el baño, el dormitorio/la habitación, el salón; la mesa, la silla, la cama, el sofá, el armario), types of housing (piso, casa, apartamento; departamento in parts of Latin America) and places in town (la plaza, la calle, el parque, el banco, la farmacia, el supermercado, la estación, el hospital, el museo).
forms: mesa, silla, cama, sofá, armario, estantería

examples.es: Mi piso tiene dos habitaciones, un baño y una cocina pequeña.
examples.en: My flat has two bedrooms, a bathroom and a small kitchen.

examples.es: En el centro hay una plaza muy bonita y muchos bares.
examples.en: In the centre there's a very pretty square and lots of bars.

mastery: Labels rooms and furniture on a plan
Describes their home in 5–6 sentences
Reads a simple flat advertisement and answers questions
commonErrors: EN: uses habitación only for "room" in general and is surprised it often means bedroom
EN: *el salón de estar mixing salón and sala de estar
boundaries: Describing places as a text is kt:es-act-describe-a1
Housing customs (living with parents, flat sharing) are sociocultural notes, not taught as facts

primitives.binding: Walk through a flat from the door: each room calls up its words; second walk-through in a different order from memory
Floor plan: learner describes it; rooms and furniture mentioned are checked against the plan

kcs.label: Weather and seasons
kcs.description: Weather uses hacer + noun (hace calor, hace frío, hace sol, hace viento, hace buen/mal tiempo), impersonal verbs (llueve, nieva) and hay/está (hay niebla, está nublado). Temperature: Estamos a 30 grados (A2). Seasons are reversed between hemispheres, and some regions have rainy and dry seasons instead.
forms: está nublado, hay niebla, hay tormenta (A2)
en verano, en invierno; la estación de lluvias

examples.es: En Buenos Aires hace frío en julio.
examples.en: In Buenos Aires it's cold in July.

examples.es: Hoy llueve y hace mucho viento.
examples.en: Today it's raining and very windy.

mastery: Matches weather symbols to expressions
Chooses hace, hay or está correctly
Gives a short weather report for two cities from a map
commonErrors: EN: *Es frío / *Está caliente for the weather (hace frío / hace calor)
EN: *Hace muy calor (mucho calor; calor is a noun)
EN: adds a subject: *Ello llueve
boundaries: tener frío (person feels cold) is kt:es-tener-sensations-doler
Climate of Hispanic countries as cultural knowledge: kt:es-lex-nature-geography

primitives.binding: Hace frío / Tengo frío / Está frío (la sopa): learner matches each to a picture (weather, person, object)
A real-style weather map/forecast; learner finds temperature and conditions for a city to plan an outfit

kcs.label: Gustar: saying what you like
kcs.description: With gustar the thing liked is the grammatical subject and the person is an indirect object: Me gusta el café (coffee pleases me). The verb agrees with the thing: me gusta + singular noun or infinitive, me gustan + plural noun. Nouns after gustar take the definite article: Me gusta la música. A1 uses mainly me/te gusta; the full set (le, nos, os, les, a mí…) follows at A2.
forms: me gusta + infinitive: Me gusta bailar.
¿Te gusta…? – Sí, mucho. / No, no mucho.
me gusta mucho / bastante / no me gusta nada (A2)

examples.es: Me gusta mucho el cine, pero no me gustan las películas de miedo.
examples.en: I like cinema a lot, but I don't like horror films.

examples.es: ¿Te gusta cocinar? – Sí, me gusta mucho.
examples.en: Do you like cooking? – Yes, I like it a lot.

mastery: Chooses gusta or gustan according to what is liked
Corrects *Yo gusto… sentences
Talks about five likes and dislikes with intensity words
commonErrors: EN: *Yo gusto el café (English subject pattern)
EN: *Me gusta las películas (agreement with the thing)
EN: drops the article: *Me gusta café
boundaries: Other persons (le, les, a ella) and encantar/interesar are kt:es-encantar-interesar
me gustaría is kt:es-fn-wishes-me-gustaria

primitives.binding: Scene: person + liked thing; learner links who feels and what pleases, then chooses gusta/gustan by the thing, not the person
Me gusta el libro / Me gustan los libros: learner picks one book or many books from the verb only

kcs.label: Agreeing and disagreeing about likes: también, tampoco, a mí sí/no
kcs.description: Reacting to someone's statement: también agrees with a positive (Me gusta. – A mí también.), tampoco agrees with a negative (No me gusta. – A mí tampoco.). To disagree: A mí sí / A mí no. With normal verbs: Yo también / Yo tampoco / Yo sí / Yo no.
forms: positive + también: Yo también. / A mí también.
negative + tampoco: Yo tampoco. / A mí tampoco.
disagree: Yo sí. / Yo no. / A mí sí. / A mí no.
with gustar use a mí, a ti…; with other verbs use yo, tú…
Sí, muy bonito. / No, no es difícil. (agreeing by repeating)

examples.es: No me gusta el fútbol. – A mí tampoco.
examples.en: I don't like football. – Neither do I.

examples.es: Yo hablo francés. – Yo no.
examples.en: I speak French. – I don't.

mastery: Chooses también vs tampoco vs sí vs no after a statement
Uses a mí with gustar and yo with other verbs
Finds a partner with the same likes in a mingle activity
commonErrors: EN: *Yo también no for "me neither" (tampoco)
EN: *Yo también after a gustar sentence (A mí también)
Latin America: también no heard in some areas; tampoco is the general form
boundaries: Full agreement/disagreement functions (estoy de acuerdo) are kt:es-fn-agree-disagree

primitives.binding: Statements positive/negative; learner wants to agree or disagree and must pick también/tampoco/sí/no; system shows the meaning of the other options
Mingle: bot states likes; learner reacts; branch continues only with a correct reaction

kcs.label: Muy, mucho, bastante, poco: degree and quantity
kcs.description: Muy intensifies adjectives and adverbs (muy alto, muy bien). Mucho modifies verbs (Trabajo mucho) and, as mucho/a/os/as, agrees with nouns (muchos amigos, mucha gente). Bastante (quite, enough) and poco (little) work the same way; un poco (a bit) softens adjectives: un poco caro.
forms: muy + adjective/adverb: muy grande, muy cerca
mucho/a/os/as + noun: mucho dinero, muchas casas
un poco + adjective: un poco difícil

examples.es: Mi ciudad es muy bonita y tiene muchos parques.
examples.en: My city is very pretty and has lots of parks.

examples.es: Estudio mucho, pero duermo poco.
examples.en: I study a lot, but I sleep little.

mastery: Chooses muy or mucho in mixed sentences
Makes mucho agree with the noun
Describes their city or habits using muy, mucho, bastante and un poco
commonErrors: EN: *mucho bonito / *muy trabajo
EN: forgets agreement: *mucho personas
EN: *muy mucho for "very much" (muchísimo)
boundaries: demasiado, todo, nada and other quantifiers are kt:es-quantifiers-indefinites
Comparatives are kt:es-comparatives

primitives.binding: Gap before adjective, verb or noun: learner must look at the next word class to choose muy or mucho/a/os/as
Place nada – poco – bastante – mucho – muchísimo on a scale, then choose the step that matches a picture

kcs.label: Free time, sport and entertainment
kcs.description: Leisure activities: leer, escuchar música, ver la tele/películas, ir al cine/al teatro/a conciertos, salir con amigos, hacer deporte, jugar al fútbol/tenis, nadar, correr, bailar, viajar. Jugar takes a + article for games and sports: jugar al fútbol (in some Latin American countries jugar fútbol).
forms: ver la tele / una película / una serie
ir al cine / al teatro / a un concierto
jugar al fútbol / al baloncesto / a las cartas
salir con amigos, ir de compras, viajar

examples.es: Los fines de semana salgo con mis amigos y juego al tenis.
examples.en: At weekends I go out with friends and play tennis.

examples.es: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? – Leo y escucho música.
examples.en: What do you do in your free time? – I read and listen to music.

mastery: Matches leisure verbs with nouns (jugar al…, hacer…, ir a…)
Answers ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? with three activities
Conducts a class survey on hobbies and reports results
commonErrors: EN: *jugar el fútbol / *tocar fútbol (jugar al fútbol; tocar is for instruments)
EN: *hacer un deporte for every sport (practicar/jugar al…)
EN: *mirar la tele is used but ver la tele is more common
boundaries: Arts and culture vocabulary is kt:es-cult-society-arts
Leisure customs (late evenings, terraces) are sociocultural notes

primitives.binding: From a short interview, learner collects verb+noun leisure chunks (jugar al…, ir a…, hacer…) into their phrase bank and uses two about themselves
Judge jugar/tocar/hacer/practicar with fútbol, guitarra, deporte, yoga; sort errors by boundary

kcs.label: Asking about and stating preferences
kcs.description: Choosing between options: ¿Té o café? – Café, por favor. Prefiero + noun or infinitive (prefiero is used as a chunk at A1). At A2: ¿Qué prefieres…?, ¿Cuál te gusta más?, Me gusta más A que B, ¿Cuál es tu… favorito/preferido?
forms: A2: Me gusta más el té que el café.

examples.es: ¿Playa o montaña? – Prefiero la montaña.
examples.en: Beach or mountains? – I prefer the mountains.

examples.es: Me gusta más leer que ver la tele.
examples.en: I like reading more than watching TV.

mastery: Picks the preferred option in short dialogues
States preferences between pairs using prefiero and me gusta más
Agrees on an activity with a partner by comparing preferences
commonErrors: EN: *Prefiero más el té (double comparison)
EN: *Me gusta mejor (más is used)
EN: *¿Qué te gusta más, A o B? fine, but *¿Cuál te gustas? confuses agreement
boundaries: The stem change in preferir is in kt:es-present-stem-change
Comparatives in general are kt:es-comparatives

primitives.binding: Pairs of options with a learner profile; learner states preference with prefiero / me gusta más and sees how each phrasing differs
Plan a weekend: each partner knows only their own preferences and must ask ¿Qué prefieres…?

kcs.label: Querer: saying what you want
kcs.description: Querer + noun or infinitive expresses wants: Quiero un café. Quiero aprender español. At A1 quiero and quieres are learned as chunks; the full e→ie pattern comes with stem-changing verbs. In shops and bars, quería (lit. "I wanted") or ¿me pone…? sounds softer than quiero.
forms: softer in service: Quería… / ¿Me pone…? (Spain) / ¿Me da…? / Me trae…

examples.es: Quiero aprender español para trabajar en Chile.
examples.en: I want to learn Spanish to work in Chile.

examples.es: ¿Quieres un café? – Sí, gracias.
examples.en: Do you want a coffee? – Yes, thanks.

mastery: Uses quiero + noun and quiero + infinitive correctly
Recognises quería as a polite request in a shop dialogue
States three wishes or wants for this year
commonErrors: EN: *Quiero a un café (personal a only before people)
EN: *Quiero que viajar (no que before infinitive)
EN: *Yo quero (stem change needed)
boundaries: Full stem-change paradigm is kt:es-present-stem-change
me gustaría for wishes is kt:es-fn-wishes-me-gustaria

primitives.binding: Collect quiero/quería/me pone/me trae chunks from café dialogues; mark which sound softer; use one in the next role play
Quiero un café / Quiero tomar un café / Quiero a mi abuela: learner picks what follows (noun, infinitive, person) and the marker needed

kcs.label: Saying yes and no: accepting, refusing, giving permission
kcs.description: Short polite responses to offers, requests and permission questions: Sí, gracias / No, (muchas) gracias; Sí, sí / Sí, claro / Vale (A2); No, lo siento. A bare No sounds abrupt; Spanish speakers soften with lo siento, gracias or a reason (A2).
forms: Sí, gracias. / No, gracias. / No, muchas gracias.
Sí, sí. / Sí, claro. (A2) / Vale. (Spain) / Okay, claro (Latin America)
A2: + reason: No, gracias, no fumo.

examples.es: ¿Más pan? – No, gracias, está bien así.
examples.en: More bread? – No thanks, I'm fine.

examples.es: ¿Puedo fumar aquí? – No, lo siento.
examples.en: Can I smoke here? – No, I'm sorry.

mastery: Chooses polite acceptances and refusals for offers
Distinguishes giving and refusing permission in short dialogues
Accepts and declines offers naturally at a dinner role play
commonErrors: EN: answers offers with *Por favor alone (Sí, por favor is fine; por favor alone is unclear)
EN: a bare No to an offer sounds rude without gracias
boundaries: Asking for permission is kt:es-poder-permission-ability; invitations and proposals are kt:es-fn-invitations

primitives.binding: Dinner at a host's home: offers, second offers and requests; learner accepts or declines; branches show the host's reaction to a bare No
Same refusal to a friend and to a host's grandmother; learner adds softeners where needed

kcs.label: Ordering in a café or restaurant
kcs.term: pedir en un bar o restaurante
kcs.description: Ordering and asking for things: Un café, por favor. Para mí, una ensalada. ¿Me pone…? (Spain) / ¿Me trae…? / ¿Me da…?; con/sin (sin azúcar); asking for the bill (La cuenta, por favor); understanding the waiter (¿Qué van a tomar? ¿Algo más?). Menú del día: primer plato, segundo plato, postre.
forms: con / sin: café con leche, agua sin gas
¿Qué van a tomar? / ¿Qué le pongo? / ¿Algo más?
de primero, de segundo, de postre

examples.es: Para mí, de primero, sopa, y de segundo, pescado. – ¿Y para beber? – Agua sin gas.
examples.en: For me, soup as a starter and fish as a main. – And to drink? – Still water.

examples.es: Perdone, la cuenta, por favor.
examples.en: Excuse me, the bill, please.

mastery: Understands a waiter's questions and the menu sections
Orders a complete meal including drinks and the bill
Handles a problem (missing dish, wrong order) with simple phrases
commonErrors: EN: *Puedo tener un café? (calque of "Can I have")
EN: *Quiero el cheque (la cuenta)
EN: orders bluntly with Dame… to a waiter, which can sound abrupt to some speakers
boundaries: Food vocabulary is kt:es-lex-food-drink; reading menus is kt:es-act-reading-signs-forms
Requests with ¿Puedes…? are kt:es-fn-requests-favours

primitives.binding: Restaurant script: greeting, menú del día choices, drinks, extra request, bill; branches when the dish is finished or the order is wrong
A real-style menú del día; learner finds a vegetarian first and second course and the price

kcs.label: Food and drink
kcs.description: Core food and drink words: el pan, la carne, el pescado, el pollo, la fruta, la verdura, el arroz, los huevos, el queso; el agua (con/sin gas), el café (solo, con leche, cortado), el té, el zumo (jugo in Latin America), la cerveza, el vino (tinto/blanco); dishes such as la tortilla, la paella, la ensalada, la sopa. Meals: el desayuno, la comida/el almuerzo, la cena.
forms: carne, pescado, pollo, fruta, verdura, pan, arroz, huevos, queso
agua con gas / sin gas, café solo / con leche, zumo (Spain) / jugo (Latin America)
tortilla (Spain: potato omelette; Mexico: maize flatbread)
A2: containers: una botella de, una lata de, un paquete de

examples.es: Para desayunar tomo café con leche y pan con tomate.
examples.en: For breakfast I have white coffee and bread with tomato.

examples.es: En México la tortilla es de maíz.
examples.en: In Mexico the tortilla is made of maize.

mastery: Sorts food words by meal and category
Reads a menu and identifies main ingredients
Describes what they usually eat in a day
commonErrors: EN: says *el agua fría es buena fine, but *la agua (el agua: el before stressed a-, still feminine)
EN: assumes tortilla means the same everywhere
EN: uses comida only for "food" and misses its Spain meaning "lunch"
boundaries: Meal times and customs are kt:es-soc-meals-timing
Containers and quantities are kt:es-quantifiers-indefinites

primitives.binding: Walk through a day of meals; each meal calls up its foods and drinks; second walk-through for a different country
Pairs zumo/jugo, patata/papa, tortilla (Spain/Mexico), comida/almuerzo: learner marks where each is used

kcs.label: When and how people eat
kcs.term: horarios y costumbres de las comidas
kcs.description: Meal times vary: in Spain lunch (la comida) is often 14:00–15:30 and dinner 21:00 or later; in many Latin American countries lunch (el almuerzo) is earlier and dinner earlier than in Spain. Tapas, la merienda (afternoon snack), el menú del día at lunchtime, and long after-meal conversation (la sobremesa) are common customs. Tipping practices differ by country.

examples.es: En España muchas personas cenan a las diez de la noche.
examples.en: In Spain many people have dinner at ten at night.

examples.es: Después de comer nos quedamos en la sobremesa una hora.
examples.en: After lunch we stay chatting at the table for an hour.

mastery: Compares meal times in Spain, one Latin American country and their own country
Interprets a scene where a visitor arrives for dinner at the "wrong" time
Explains what tapas, merienda and menú del día are
commonErrors: EN: plans to have dinner at 18:00 in Spain and finds restaurants closed
EN: assumes one schedule for all Spanish-speaking countries
boundaries: These are tendencies by region, age and work pattern, not rules
Food vocabulary is kt:es-lex-food-drink

primitives.binding: Visitor invites Spanish colleagues to dinner at 18:30 and nobody is hungry; learner explains and reschedules
Meal times table for Spain, Mexico, Argentina and the learner's country; learner predicts then checks

kcs.label: Shopping: asking for things and prices
kcs.description: Shop exchanges: ¿Tienen…? ¿Cuánto cuesta / cuestan? ¿Cuánto es? Es muy caro / barato. Talla (clothes) and número (shoes); ¿Puedo probármelo? (A2); paying: en efectivo, con tarjeta. Clothes: camisa, camiseta, pantalones, falda, vestido, jersey, zapatos.
forms: ¿Cuánto cuesta este jersey? / ¿Cuánto cuestan estos zapatos?
la talla M, la 40; el número 38 (shoes)
shops: supermercado, mercado, panadería, farmacia, tienda de ropa

examples.en: How much are these oranges? – Two euros a kilo.

The full model transaction is kt:es-act-transactional

kcs.label: Numbers above 100, prices and years
kcs.description: Cien (exactly 100) vs ciento (101–199: ciento uno). Hundreds agree with feminine nouns: doscientas personas. Mil is invariable (dos mil); un millón de + noun. Years are read as a full number: 2026 = dos mil veintiséis. Spanish writes decimals with a comma (1,5) and groups thousands with a point or a space (15.000 / 15 000); prices: 3,50 €.
forms: cien / ciento uno … ciento noventa y nueve
years: mil novecientos noventa y nueve, dos mil veintiséis

examples.es: Este ordenador cuesta seiscientos cincuenta euros.
examples.en: This computer costs six hundred and fifty euros.

examples.es: Mi abuela nació en mil novecientos cuarenta y ocho.
examples.en: My grandmother was born in nineteen forty-eight.

mastery: Writes large numbers and prices heard aloud
Reads years and prices aloud correctly
Converts written figures to words and back, including decimal commas
commonErrors: EN: *ciento euros (cien euros)
EN: reads years in pairs: *diecinueve noventa y nueve
EN: *quinientos personas (quinientas)
EN: writes 1.5 for one and a half (1,5)
boundaries: 0–100 is kt:es-numbers-0-100
Different number groupings are a feature for learners from other writing systems too

primitives.binding: Convert between figures and words for prices and years; learner first estimates, then writes, then reads aloud; system marks decimal comma and thousands point
Price announcements and years in a short biography; learner fills a table

kcs.label: Service encounters: simple transactions
kcs.description: Carrying out a complete service exchange face to face: greeting, saying what you need, answering the assistant's questions, choosing, paying, thanking and closing. At A1 with simple purchases and directions; at A2 also in hotels, stations, tourist offices, banks and post offices.
forms: greeting → request → clarification → choice → price → payment → thanks → goodbye
closing: Hasta luego, que tenga un buen día.

examples.es: Buenos días. ¿Qué desea? – Quería un billete para Toledo. – ¿Ida y vuelta? – Sí, por favor.
examples.en: Good morning. What would you like? – I'd like a ticket to Toledo. – Return? – Yes, please.

examples.es: ¿Algo más? – No, nada más. ¿Cuánto es? – Doce euros. – Aquí tiene.
examples.en: Anything else? – No, nothing else. How much is it? – Twelve euros. – Here you are.

mastery: Follows the stages of a recorded transaction and notes the outcome
Completes an unscripted purchase in a role play with an assistant who asks follow-up questions
Recovers when the assistant offers an alternative or misunderstands
commonErrors: EN: skips the greeting and goes straight to the request, which can sound abrupt
EN: answers ¿Algo más? with *No, gracias, es todo — fine; but freezes when asked an unexpected question
boundaries: Phone transactions are kt:es-fn-telephone
Specific functions (ordering, shopping) are kt:es-fn-ordering-food and kt:es-fn-shopping-prices

primitives.binding: Full transaction with branching assistant (out of stock, other size, card not accepted); every stage of the model sequence must be completed
Learner labels each turn of a recorded transaction with its stage (greeting, request, options, price, payment, closing)

kcs.label: Ir and venir: going and coming
kcs.description: Ir (voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van) = go, venir (vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen) = come towards the speaker. ir a + place (Voy al trabajo); ir en + transport (en metro, en coche) but a pie / andando; venir de + place. Spanish uses ir, not venir, when moving towards the listener: Ya voy (I'm coming).
forms: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van
vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen
ir a + place: Voy a la playa / al centro
ir en + transport: en autobús, en tren; a pie

examples.es: Voy a clase en metro, pero vuelvo a pie.
examples.en: I go to class by metro but come back on foot.

examples.es: ¿Vienes a la fiesta? – Sí, voy.
examples.en: Are you coming to the party? – Yes, I'm coming.

mastery: Conjugates ir and venir in all persons
Chooses ir or venir from the speaker's position
Explains how they get to school or work
commonErrors: EN: *Vengo when going towards the listener (Voy)
EN: *ir por coche / *en pie (en coche, a pie)
EN: drops a: *Voy la playa
boundaries: ir a + infinitive (future) is kt:es-ir-a-infinitive; llevar/traer is kt:es-deixis-llevar-traer

primitives.binding: Map with speaker and listener; learner moves a character and must choose ir or venir from the speaker's position, including Ya voy
ir and venir grids, then new subjects; irregular forms highlighted

kcs.label: Prepositions a, en, de, con, sin, para: basic uses
kcs.description: High-frequency prepositions: a for direction and time (voy a Lima, a las ocho), en for location and transport (en casa, en tren), de for origin, possession and material (soy de Bogotá, la casa de Ana), con/sin (with/without), para + destination or person (para mí). a + el → al, de + el → del.
forms: a: direction, time: Voy a Madrid. A las tres.
en: place, transport, month: en casa, en coche, en mayo
de: origin, possession: de Chile, de mi madre
con / sin: con leche, sin azúcar

examples.es: Vivo en Quito, pero soy de Guayaquil.
examples.en: I live in Quito, but I'm from Guayaquil.

examples.es: Este regalo es para mi madre.
examples.en: This present is for my mother.

mastery: Chooses a/en/de in mixed sentences about places and transport
Uses al/del in all required contexts
Describes a journey with origin, destination and transport
commonErrors: EN: *Estoy a casa (en casa)
EN: *Vivo a Madrid (en)
EN: *por coche (en coche)
boundaries: por vs para is kt:es-por-para-basic; place phrases like al lado de are kt:es-place-expressions

primitives.binding: Journey picture: link origin, destination, transport and companion to de / a / en / con
Judge sentences with en/a after estar, vivir, ir, llegar (llegar a vs llegar en is a common trap) and sort errors

kcs.label: Ordinal numbers 1st–10th
kcs.description: Ordinals primero … décimo agree in gender and number (la segunda calle) and usually go before the noun. Primero and tercero drop -o before a masculine singular noun: el primer piso, el tercer día. Written 1.º, 2.ª. Used for floors, streets, order and courses.
forms: primero/a, segundo/a, tercero/a, cuarto/a, quinto/a, sexto/a, séptimo/a, octavo/a, noveno/a, décimo/a
primer, tercer before masculine singular noun

examples.es: Gire en la tercera calle a la izquierda.
examples.en: Turn into the third street on the left.

examples.es: Vivo en el primer piso, puerta B.
examples.en: I live on the first floor, door B.

mastery: Matches ordinals with abbreviations
Uses primer/tercer before masculine nouns
Gives and follows floor and street directions
commonErrors: EN: *el primero piso (primer)
EN: forgets agreement: *la segundo calle
EN: uses ordinals for dates: *el tercero de mayo (cardinals: el tres de mayo; el primero de mayo is fine in many varieties)
boundaries: Directions are kt:es-fn-directions-basic

primitives.binding: Building plan; hear "La señora vive en el quinto, puerta C" and tap the flat
Rule: agree in gender; primero/tercero shorten before masculine singular; apply to unseen phrases

kcs.label: Asking for and understanding simple directions
kcs.description: Asking where a place is and following simple directions: ¿Dónde está…? ¿Hay un… por aquí? ¿Está lejos? Directions use present or imperative chunks: todo recto, a la derecha, a la izquierda, la primera/segunda calle, está cerca/lejos, a cinco minutos.
forms: ¿Está lejos? – No, está a cinco minutos (andando).
todo recto / derecho (parts of Latin America)
a la derecha / a la izquierda
chunks: sigue, gira, cruza (taught fully at A2)

examples.es: Perdone, ¿hay una farmacia por aquí? – Sí, todo recto y la segunda a la derecha.
examples.en: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here? – Yes, straight on and the second on the right.

examples.es: ¿Está lejos el museo? – No, está a diez minutos andando.
examples.en: Is the museum far? – No, it's ten minutes' walk.

mastery: Follows spoken directions on a map to the right place
Asks for a place politely and checks distance
Gives simple directions from the school to a nearby place
commonErrors: EN: *Perdón, ¿dónde es la farmacia? (está)
EN: confuses derecho (straight on in parts of Latin America) with a la derecha (right)
boundaries: Full imperative instructions are kt:es-fn-directions-a2

primitives.binding: Street map: hear directions and trace the route; the end point is the evidence
Each partner has a map with different places marked; they must ask ¿Dónde está…? and mark the answers

kcs.label: Transport and travel
kcs.description: Transport and travel words: el autobús (camión in Mexico, colectivo in Argentina), el metro, el tren, el avión, el taxi, el coche/carro/auto, la bici; la estación, la parada, el aeropuerto; el billete (Spain) / boleto (Latin America), de ida, de ida y vuelta; el hotel, la habitación doble/individual, la maleta, el pasaporte.
forms: billete (ES) / boleto (LatAm), de ida / de ida y vuelta
A2: reservar, hacer una reserva, perder el tren

examples.es: Un billete de ida y vuelta para Sevilla, por favor.
examples.en: A return ticket to Seville, please.

examples.es: Quería una habitación doble con baño para dos noches.
examples.en: I'd like a double room with a bathroom for two nights.

mastery: Matches transport words, including regional variants
Buys a ticket and books a room in role plays
Reads a simple timetable or booking confirmation
commonErrors: EN: asks for a *tíquet de tren (billete/boleto; tique is used for receipts and some tickets)
EN: *coger in some Latin American countries is vulgar; tomar el autobús is safe everywhere
boundaries: Transport systems and famous airports/airlines are cultural notes in kt:es-cult-countries-capitals

primitives.binding: autobús/camión/colectivo/guagua, billete/boleto, coger/tomar: learner marks where each is used and which is safe everywhere
Ticket office: destination, one-way or return, time, platform; branches for sold-out trains

kcs.label: Saber and conocer: knowing facts, skills, people and places
kcs.description: Saber (sé, sabes, sabe…) = know facts or information and know how to do something (Sé nadar). Conocer (conozco, conoces, conoce…) = be acquainted with people, places and things (Conozco Bolivia. Conozco a Leticia). Saber + infinitive also expresses learned ability.
forms: sé, sabes, sabe, sabemos, sabéis, saben
conozco, conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocéis, conocen
saber + fact / que…: Sé que es inglesa. (A2)
conocer a + person: Conozco a tu hermano.

examples.es: ¿Sabes cocinar? – Sí, sé hacer una paella muy buena.
examples.en: Can you cook? – Yes, I can make a very good paella.

examples.es: No conozco Granada, pero conozco a una chica de allí.
examples.en: I don't know Granada, but I know a girl from there.

mastery: Chooses saber or conocer in mixed sentences
Uses conocer a with people
Asks classmates what they know how to do and which places they know
commonErrors: EN: uses saber for people: *Sé a tu hermano
EN: *Conozco nadar
EN: *sabo / *conoco for sé / conozco
boundaries: poder (ability depending on circumstances) is kt:es-poder-permission-ability
Remembering (acordarse) is kt:es-acordarse

primitives.binding: Gaps followed by a fact, a skill, a person or a place; learner must read what follows to choose saber or conocer
Find someone who sabe… / conoce…; questions must use the right verb to be answered

kcs.label: Giving and asking for opinions
kcs.description: Giving an opinion softly with (Yo) creo que + clause, asking ¿Y tú? or tagging ¿no?; at A2 also Para mí… and ¿Crees que…? Creo que also softens uncertain information: Creo que la clase es a las cinco.

examples.es: Creo que el español es más fácil que el francés, ¿y tú?
examples.en: I think Spanish is easier than French, what about you?

examples.es: Es muy bonito, pero creo que es un poco caro.
examples.en: It's very nice, but I think it's a bit expensive.

mastery: Identifies opinion vs fact in short statements
Gives opinions on three topics with creo que
Takes part in a short opinion exchange using ¿y tú? and sí, pero…
commonErrors: EN: *Pienso de que… / *Creo de que (no de)
EN: drops que: *Creo es caro
EN: *En mi opinión used everywhere; correct but heavy in casual speech
boundaries: Agreeing and disagreeing at A2 (estoy de acuerdo) is kt:es-fn-agree-disagree
Certainty and doubt (estoy seguro) are kt:es-fn-certainty

primitives.binding: Opinion turns on everyday topics (city vs countryside); learner gives opinion with creo que, asks back, and counters with sí, pero…
Same disagreement said bluntly (Es caro.) and softened (Creo que es un poco caro, ¿no?); learner marks which fits talking to a host

kcs.label: Evaluating things: good, bad, easy, interesting
kcs.description: Evaluating with ser + adjective (Es muy interesante, Es un poco difícil), adverbs (bien, mal, regular, así así), and at A2 estar bien/mal for judging results (Esto está muy bien), ¡Qué + adjective! (kt:es-exclamatives-que) and no es nada + adjective. Asking: ¿Está bien? ¿Qué tal el…? (A2).
forms: fácil, difícil, interesante, aburrido, útil, importante, normal
A2: Está bien / Está mal (result, correctness)

examples.es: El museo es muy interesante, pero el restaurante es regular.
examples.en: The museum is very interesting, but the restaurant is so-so.

examples.es: ¿Qué tal el examen? – Bastante bien.
examples.en: How was the exam? – Pretty good.

mastery: Places evaluations on a good–bad scale
Evaluates five places or activities with intensifiers
Asks for and gives quick evaluations (¿Qué tal…?) about a trip or class
commonErrors: EN: *Es bueno for "it's fine/OK" where Está bien is expected
EN: *muy fantástico (fantástico is already extreme)
boundaries: Feelings are kt:es-fn-feelings; comparison is kt:es-comparatives
ser vs estar with adjectives is kt:es-ser-vs-estar

primitives.binding: Put fatal – mal – regular – bien – muy bien – estupendo on a scale; then pick the step matching each review
Photos of a hotel, a meal and a beach; learner evaluates each; check adjectives agree and intensifiers are used

kcs.label: Saying something is possible
kcs.description: Expressing possibility and doubt simply: Es posible. Quizá(s). No sé. At A2 also Es probable, Puede ser, Depende. At A2 quizá is used with the indicative in simple sentences (Quizá ha recibido una mala noticia); the subjunctive after quizá is a B1 topic.
forms: A2: Es probable. / Puede ser. / Depende.

examples.es: Creo que el museo cierra los lunes. – Sí, es posible.
examples.en: I think the museum closes on Mondays. – Yes, it's possible.

examples.es: ¿Vienes mañana? – No sé… quizá.
examples.en: Are you coming tomorrow? – I don't know… maybe.

mastery: Places possibility expressions on a likelihood scale
Responds to uncertain statements with an appropriate expression
Speculates about a picture using es posible, quizá, puede ser
commonErrors: EN: *Puede ser que + indicative (subjunctive is needed after puede ser que; at A2 use Puede ser alone)
EN: *Tal vez sí que… overused; simple quizá is enough
boundaries: Subjunctive after quizá, es posible que is B1
Certainty (estoy seguro) is kt:es-fn-certainty

primitives.binding: Rank seguro – probable – posible – quizá – no sé; then choose the step that matches a speaker's evidence
Ambiguous picture (a person running with a suitcase); learner speculates; check at least two possibility markers

kcs.label: Showing you are listening and managing turns
kcs.description: Listeners in Spanish give frequent feedback: Sí, sí; Ajá; ¿Sí?; ¿De verdad?; ¡Qué bien!; repeating a word as an echo question (¿Un caftán?). At A2 also interrupting politely (Perdón, …) and inviting a story (¿Qué tal el viaje?).
forms: A2: ¿Qué tal el fin de semana? – Muy bien, fuimos a…

examples.es: Ayer vi a Shakira en el aeropuerto. – ¿De verdad? ¿Dónde?
examples.en: Yesterday I saw Shakira at the airport. – Really? Where?

examples.es: Mañana no hay clase. – ¿Mañana? ¡Qué bien!
examples.en: There's no class tomorrow. – Tomorrow? Great!

mastery: Identifies backchannel signals in a recorded conversation
Uses at least three different signals while listening to a partner's story
Uses an echo question to check a surprising detail
commonErrors: EN: stays silent while listening, which Spanish speakers may read as lack of interest
EN: uses English "uh-huh / OK" instead of Spanish signals
boundaries: Repair when not understanding is kt:es-str-repair-basic
Telephone conventions are kt:es-fn-telephone

primitives.binding: Learner listens to a story told in chunks and must react at each pause; absent or misplaced reactions are logged
Friend tells weekend news; learner keeps it going with echo questions and ¿De verdad?

kcs.label: Why and because: por qué / porque
kcs.description: ¿Por qué? (two words, accent) asks for a reason; porque (one word, no accent) gives it, normally after the main clause at A1. At A2 por + noun also gives a cause (Trabajo por dinero).
forms: ¿Por qué estudias español? – Porque quiero viajar.
A2: por + noun: por el tráfico

examples.es: ¿Por qué no vienes? – Porque estoy cansado.
examples.en: Why aren't you coming? – Because I'm tired.

examples.es: Estudio español porque mi pareja es de Cuba.
examples.en: I study Spanish because my partner is from Cuba.

mastery: Spells por qué and porque correctly in context
Answers why-questions with porque + full clause
Writes three reasons for learning Spanish
commonErrors: EN: writes *porqué or *por que in answers
EN: writes the question as *¿Porque estudias…? (por qué)
boundaries: como (since) and por eso (so) are kt:es-por-eso-entonces
el porqué (noun) is beyond A2

primitives.binding: Sentences where only the spelling (por qué / porque) shows question or answer; learner chooses
Two facts (no vengo / estoy enfermo); learner joins with porque and splits back, seeing which is cause

kcs.label: Purpose: para + infinitive
kcs.description: Para + infinitive expresses purpose when the subject is the same: Estudio español para trabajar en México. ¿Para qué…? asks for the purpose (A2). Para + noun also gives use or destination: El boli es para escribir. Es para ti.
forms: para + infinitive: para aprender, para viajar
thing + es para + infinitive: Es para abrir botellas.

examples.es: Voy a la biblioteca para estudiar.
examples.en: I go to the library to study.

examples.es: ¿Para qué es esto? – Es para cortar el pan.
examples.en: What's this for? – It's for cutting bread.

mastery: Distinguishes cause (porque) from purpose (para) in short texts
Completes sentences with para + infinitive
Explains the use of five objects
commonErrors: EN: *por aprender for purpose (para)
EN: *para que aprender (no que before infinitive)
EN: *para + -ing form (para estudiando)
boundaries: para que + subjunctive is B1; por vs para is kt:es-por-para-basic

primitives.binding: Same action, two continuations: learner wants to give a reason or a purpose and chooses porque or para
Objects (abrebotellas, paraguas, llave); learner explains each with es para + infinitive

kcs.label: Relative clauses with que
kcs.description: Que joins a clause to a noun to identify it: La chica que lleva gafas es mi prima. El libro que leo es muy interesante. Que is invariable and works for people and things, as subject or object. At A1 the relative clause is in the present indicative; past and future indicative follow at A2.
forms: noun + que + verb: el chico que vive aquí
noun + que + subject + verb: la casa que tengo
A2: past tenses in the clause: la película que vimos

examples.es: El restaurante que está en la plaza es muy caro.
examples.en: The restaurant that is in the square is very expensive.

examples.es: ¿Es este el libro que necesitas?
examples.en: Is this the book (that) you need?

mastery: Identifies people in a picture from que-clauses
Combines two sentences into one with que
Describes objects or people for a partner to identify
commonErrors: EN: omits que as in English: *El libro leo es bueno
EN: uses *quien as a subject relative in defining clauses (*la chica quien vive)
boundaries: Relatives with prepositions, donde and lo que are B1
Interrogative qué is kt:es-interrogatives-basic

primitives.binding: Two sentences (Tengo un amigo. Mi amigo vive en Cádiz.) combined with que and split back; learner sees what que replaces
Crowd picture; learner identifies people with que-clauses; partner must find the person described

kcs.label: Infinitive after verbs and as a noun
kcs.description: The infinitive (-ar, -er, -ir) follows verbs like querer, poder, saber, necesitar, preferir, gustar (Quiero ir, Me gusta bailar) and can be a subject (Estudiar idiomas es útil) or a short answer (¿Qué haces? – Estudiar). Some verbs need a preposition: aprender a, empezar a, volver a (A2). Past participles also work as adjectives: cansado, cerrado.
forms: infinitive as subject: Hablar español es útil.
participle as adjective: Estoy cansado. La tienda está cerrada.

examples.es: Necesito comprar pan.
examples.en: I need to buy bread.

examples.es: Leer en español es difícil, pero muy útil.
examples.en: Reading in Spanish is difficult but very useful.

mastery: Chooses infinitive rather than conjugated form after querer, poder, gustar
Uses an infinitive as subject of ser + adjective
Talks about things they want to, need to and can do
commonErrors: EN: uses the gerund for English -ing: *Me gusta nadando
EN: conjugates both verbs: *Quiero voy
EN: adds *a after querer: *Quiero a ir
boundaries: Perífrasis ir a, tener que, acabar de are separate KCs
Gerund is kt:es-estar-gerund

primitives.binding: Sentences where the second verb must be infinitive, conjugated or participle; learner checks what the first verb requires
Judge Me gusta bailar / *Me gusta bailando / Quiero ir / *Quiero voy and sort into error types

kcs.label: Syllables and word stress
kcs.description: Spanish syllables tend to be open (ca-sa). Every word has one stressed syllable; stress can change meaning (papa/papá, término/termino/terminó). Rule of thumb: words ending in a vowel, -n or -s stress the second-to-last syllable (ca-sa, ha-blan); other words stress the last (ha-blar, re-loj). Exceptions carry a written accent.
forms: stress changes meaning: papa / papá; hablo / habló

examples.es: La música de este teléfono es muy rápida.
examples.en: The music on this phone is very fast.

examples.es: Hablo con mi papá, no con el papa.
examples.en: I'm talking to my dad, not to the pope.

mastery: Hears and marks the stressed syllable in two- and three-syllable words
Predicts stress from spelling using the default rule
Reads aloud new words with correct stress
commonErrors: EN: transfers English stress from cognates: *TE-le-fo-no for te-LÉ-fo-no, *HOS-pi-tal for hos-pi-TAL
EN: reduces unstressed syllables
boundaries: Written accent rules are kt:es-orth-written-accents
Rhythm and linking are kt:es-phon-rhythm-linking

primitives.binding: Stress minimal pairs papa/papá, hablo/habló, término/termino/terminó; learner picks what was heard, then produces each
Learner marks the stressed syllable on a syllable grid while listening, then reads following the grid

kcs.label: Rhythm, pauses and linking words
kcs.description: Spanish has a fairly even syllable-timed rhythm. Words are linked within a breath group: a final consonant joins the next vowel (los_amigos → lo-sa-mi-gos) and vowels merge (me_he levantado). Speakers pause at commas and full stops; lists have one breath group per item.
forms: pauses at punctuation; lists: tengo un lápiz, | un cuaderno | y un libro

examples.es: Tengo dos amigos en Alicante.
examples.en: I have two friends in Alicante.

examples.es: Mis amigos y yo vamos a Ecuador.
examples.en: My friends and I are going to Ecuador.

mastery: Marks links and pauses in a short transcript
Shadows a recorded sentence matching rhythm and linking
Reads a short text aloud with natural linking and pauses
commonErrors: EN: stress-timed rhythm, squashing unstressed syllables
EN: inserts glottal stops between words starting with vowels
boundaries: Intonation is kt:es-phon-intonation

primitives.binding: Learner marks pauses and links on a transcript, shadows the audio and compares their pause curve with the model
Dictation of linked speech (Va a ir a Alicante); learner aligns what they wrote with the original to see where linking hid word boundaries

kcs.label: Written accent marks (tildes)
kcs.description: The written accent marks a stressed syllable that breaks the default rule: agudas ending in vowel, -n, -s (café, canción, inglés), llanas ending in other consonants (árbol, fácil) and all esdrújulas (música). It also distinguishes pairs of one-syllable words: tú/tu, él/el, sí/si, sé/se, té/te, mí/mi, and question words (qué, dónde). Capitals keep their accents (ÁNGEL).
forms: llanas with other endings: fácil, lápiz, árbol
diacritics: tú/tu, él/el, té/te, sé/se, sí/si, mí/mi (A2)
question words: qué, quién, cómo, dónde, cuándo, cuánto

examples.es: ¿Tú tienes tu móvil? – Sí, aquí está.
examples.en: Do you have your phone? – Yes, here it is.

examples.es: Él compra el té en el mercado.
examples.en: He buys the tea at the market.

mastery: Explains why given words carry or lack an accent
Adds missing accents to a short text
Chooses tú/tu, él/el, sí/si by meaning
commonErrors: EN: omits all accents as optional decoration
EN: puts accents on every stressed syllable (*cása)
EN: confuses tu/tú and el/él in writing
boundaries: Stress itself is kt:es-phon-stress-syllables
Accent rules for diphthongs and hiatus (día, país) are introduced as words; full rules are B1

primitives.binding: Learner's own text: first pass fixes only esdrújulas, second pass only diacritic pairs (tú/tu, él/el)
Rule: default stress → accent only when broken; apply to unseen words and show each decision step

kcs.label: Capital letters, punctuation and abbreviations
kcs.description: Capitals for names, places, institutions and after a full stop; lower case for days, months, nationalities, languages and titles in running text (el señor García). Punctuation: no comma between subject and verb; comma in lists before the last item is not used before y; colon after a letter greeting (Querida Ana:); dash for dialogue (—¿Vienes? —Sí.). Common abbreviations and symbols: Sr., Sra., D./D.ª, Ud., c/, n.º, tfno., €, km, @.
forms: lower case: lunes, enero, español, señor
no comma before y in a simple list: pan, leche y huevos
colon after greeting in letters: Querido Juan:
abbreviations: Sr., Sra., Ud./Vd., c/ (calle), n.º, pág., tfno.

examples.es: El lunes 3 de marzo voy a la c/ Mayor, n.º 12.
examples.en: On Monday 3 March I'm going to 12 Mayor Street.

examples.es: Querida Lucía: Te escribo desde Lima…
examples.en: Dear Lucía, I'm writing to you from Lima…

mastery: Corrects capitalisation in a text with days, months, languages and names
Punctuates a short dialogue and a letter opening
Reads common abbreviations on forms and addresses
commonErrors: EN: capitalises days, months, languages and nationalities
EN: puts a comma after the letter greeting (Querida Ana, …) – a colon is standard
EN: Oxford comma before y
boundaries: Inverted marks are kt:es-orth-inverted-marks; written accents are kt:es-orth-written-accents

primitives.binding: Learner's own postcard: one pass for capitals and lower case, one for punctuation, one for abbreviations
Real-style forms, envelopes and signs; learner finds and expands abbreviations (c/, n.º, Sra., tfno.)

kcs.label: Reading signs, timetables, menus and forms
kcs.description: Reading short public texts to get what you need: signs (Entrada, Salida, Abierto, Cerrado, Prohibido fumar, Empujar/Tirar), timetables and opening hours, menus, tickets, tourist leaflets, and simple forms with personal data. Using a bilingual dictionary to check key words.
forms: entrada / salida, abierto / cerrado, empujar / tirar
horario: de lunes a viernes, de 9:00 a 14:00
menú del día, primer plato, segundo plato, postre, bebida
formulario: nombre, apellidos, fecha de nacimiento, domicilio, firma
billete: origen, destino, salida, llegada, vagón, asiento

examples.es: Rellene el formulario con sus datos personales.

boundaries: Longer texts (ads, news, stories) are kt:es-act-reading-a2

kcs.label: Writing short messages, notes and postcards

message: ¿Quedamos a las 7 en la plaza?

kcs.label: Describing a person, object or place (A1)
kcs.description: Producing a short spoken or written description that goes from general to particular: first anchor (who/what/where), then features (appearance, size, colour, parts, what there is) using ser, tener, llevar, hay, estar and the present tense.
forms: anchor: Es mi amigo Carlos. / Mi casa está en…
features: es alto, tiene el pelo…, lleva…
places: hay un baño, una cocina…; está cerca de…
objects: es rojo, es de plástico (A2), es para…

examples.es: Mi habitación es pequeña. Hay una cama, una mesa y un armario blanco. La ventana está al lado de la cama.
examples.en: My room is small. There is a bed, a table and a white wardrobe. The window is next to the bed.

examples.es: Mi amiga Rosa es baja y morena, tiene los ojos negros y siempre lleva vaqueros.
examples.en: My friend Rosa is short and dark-haired, has black eyes and always wears jeans.

mastery: Orders the sentences of a jumbled description from general to particular
Writes a 40–60 word description of a person, object or room
Gives a 30-second spoken description of a photo

kcs.label: Listening to slow, clear everyday speech (A1)
kcs.description: Understanding very short, slow, clearly articulated speech on familiar topics: numbers, prices, times, names, simple instructions and short face-to-face exchanges about people and places, with pauses and repetition.
forms: key data: numbers, prices, times, names
short instructions: Abre el libro. Gira a la derecha.
short conversations about people and places
strategies: listen for key words, ask for repetition

examples.es: El tren para Valencia sale a las diez y cuarto del andén tres.
examples.en: The train to Valencia leaves at quarter past ten from platform three.

examples.es: Hola, soy Marta, la vecina del segundo. ¿Tienes un poco de sal?
examples.en: Hi, I'm Marta, the neighbour from the second floor. Do you have a little salt?

mastery: Notes numbers, times and names from short recordings
Follows a sequence of simple spoken instructions
Answers gist questions about a very short dialogue
commonErrors: EN: tries to understand every word and loses the thread
EN: misses information because of linking between words
boundaries: A2 listening (announcements, short presentations) is kt:es-act-listening-a2

primitives.binding: Short announcements and dialogues; only the target slots are recorded; errors classified by number, time or name
After answering, learner writes what they heard for one sentence and aligns it with the transcript

kcs.label: Short spoken presentations about oneself (A1)

examples.en: Hi, my name is Kenji, I'm Japanese and I live in Madrid. I work in a hotel and at weekends I play football.

kcs.label: Stem-changing verbs in the present: e→ie, o→ue, e→i, u→ue
kcs.term: verbos con diptongo y cambio vocálico
kcs.description: In many verbs the stressed stem vowel changes in all persons except nosotros and vosotros: querer → quiero, poder → puedo, pedir → pido, jugar → juego. The endings stay regular. Frequent verbs: e→ie querer, preferir, empezar, cerrar, pensar, entender, tener (tienes), venir (vienes); o→ue poder, volver, dormir, costar, encontrar, acostarse; e→i pedir, repetir, servir, vestirse; u→ue jugar.
forms: e→ie: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren
o→ue: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden
e→i: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden
u→ue: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan
dictionaries often mark these as querer (ie), poder (ue), pedir (i)

examples.es: ¿A qué hora empieza la película? – Empieza a las nueve y vuelvo a las once.
examples.en: What time does the film start? – It starts at nine and I get back at eleven.

examples.es: Mis hijos duermen poco, pero nosotros dormimos bien.
examples.en: My children sleep little, but we sleep well.

mastery: Identifies which forms of a stem-changing verb change and which do not
Conjugates unseen stem-changing verbs marked (ie), (ue), (i)
Describes their routine and preferences using at least six stem-changing verbs
commonErrors: EN: changes nosotros too: *queremos ok but *pueremos / *duermimos
EN: forgets the change: *podo, *quero, *jugo
EN: applies e→ie to e→i verbs: *piedo
boundaries: Irregular yo forms (tengo, hago) are kt:es-present-irregular-yo
Stem changes in the preterite (pidió, durmió) are B1

primitives.binding: Learner derives "stressed stem vowel changes, nosotros/vosotros don't" from querer and poder, then applies it to unseen verbs (cerrar, volver, servir) step by step
Sentences where only the stem shows the person (podemos / pueden); learner identifies the subject

kcs.label: Verbs irregular in the yo form
kcs.description: A group of frequent verbs is irregular only in the yo form: hacer → hago, poner → pongo, salir → salgo, traer → traigo, ver → veo, dar → doy, saber → sé, conocer → conozco (and other -cer/-cir verbs: conduzco, traduzco). Tener, venir and decir combine an irregular yo (tengo, vengo, digo) with a stem change in other forms.
forms: -go: hago, pongo, salgo, traigo, tengo, vengo, digo, oigo
decir: digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen

examples.es: Salgo de casa a las ocho y hago la compra después del trabajo.
examples.en: I leave home at eight and do the shopping after work.

examples.es: ¿Qué dices? No te oigo.
examples.en: What are you saying? I can't hear you.

mastery: Supplies the yo form of 15 frequent verbs
Answers questions in the first person using irregular forms
Writes a paragraph about their typical day using at least five irregular yo verbs
commonErrors: EN: regularises: *hacio, *salo, *conoco, *pono
EN: carries the -g- into other persons: *hages, *salges
boundaries: Stem changes are kt:es-present-stem-change; ser, estar, ir, haber are taught at A1

primitives.binding: Group verbs by pattern (-go, -oy, -zco); learner predicts the yo form of unseen members (componer, suponer, reconocer)
Infinitive shown; learner types the yo form before it is revealed; first attempt and hint use logged separately

kcs.label: How often: frequency expressions and habits
kcs.description: The present tense describes habits; frequency is expressed with siempre, casi siempre, normalmente, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca, nunca, and with todos los días, una vez a la semana, dos veces al mes. Nunca can go before the verb (Nunca bebo café) or after it with no (No bebo nunca café). Soler + infinitive (Suelo cenar tarde) also expresses habit.
forms: siempre, normalmente, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca, nunca
todos los días / todas las semanas
una vez / dos veces a la semana, al mes, al año

examples.es: Voy al gimnasio dos veces a la semana, pero nunca voy los domingos.
examples.en: I go to the gym twice a week, but I never go on Sundays.

examples.es: ¿Con qué frecuencia comes fuera? – A veces, los viernes.
examples.en: How often do you eat out? – Sometimes, on Fridays.

mastery: Places frequency adverbs on a scale
Uses nunca in both positions correctly
Reports a partner's habits from a frequency survey
commonErrors: EN: *No nunca voy or *Nunca no voy
EN: *dos tiempos a la semana (veces)
EN: *usualmente overused; normalmente is more common
boundaries: Double negation in general is kt:es-double-negation
Habitual past (imperfect) is kt:es-imperfect

primitives.binding: Put siempre – a menudo – a veces – casi nunca – nunca on a ladder, then place each person's habit from a diary
Frequency survey: learner asks ¿Con qué frecuencia…? and records answers in a grid

kcs.description: Jobs (médico/a, profesor/a, abogado/a, camarero/a, dependiente/a, enfermero/a, ingeniero/a, funcionario/a), workplaces (oficina, empresa, tienda, fábrica, hospital), studies (asignaturas, examen, aprobar/suspender, la universidad, el instituto, el colegio) and phrases such as trabajar de/en, estar en paro, estar jubilado, buscar trabajo, hacer una entrevista.

buscar trabajo, tener una entrevista, enviar el currículum
asignaturas: Matemáticas, Historia; aprobar / suspender un examen

examples.es: Mañana tengo un examen de Historia y no quiero suspender.

mastery: Matches jobs with workplaces and tasks
Describes their job or studies in 6–8 sentences
Reads a simple job ad and answers questions

Classroom language is kt:es-lex-classroom

kcs.label: Estar + adjective for states and conditions
kcs.description: Estar + adjective or participle describes a state or condition, often the result of a change: Estoy cansado. La tienda está cerrada. El café está frío. Some adjectives are used mainly with estar (contento, enfadado, preocupado, enfermo, sentado/de pie) and agree like any adjective.
forms: estar + cansado, contento, nervioso, enfadado, preocupado, triste
estar + participle: abierto, cerrado, roto, sentado

examples.es: Estoy muy cansada porque hoy he trabajado mucho.
examples.en: I'm very tired because I've worked a lot today.

examples.es: El museo está cerrado los lunes.
examples.en: The museum is closed on Mondays.

mastery: Chooses estar for states in mixed sentences
Makes estar + adjective agree with the subject
Says how people in pictures feel and why
commonErrors: EN: *Soy cansado / *Soy enfermo for temporary states
EN: forgets agreement: *Ellas están cansado
boundaries: The ser/estar contrast with the same adjective is kt:es-ser-vs-estar
Emotions as functions are kt:es-fn-feelings

primitives.binding: Pictures of people and places (tired runner, closed shop); learner describes with estar + adjective; agreement and estar choice checked
Same adjective with different subjects (La sopa está fría / Estoy frío? → Tengo frío) to show which combinations exist

kcs.label: Ser or estar with adjectives
kcs.description: Ser + adjective classifies or describes what someone/something is like (Es alto, Es simpático, La casa es grande). Estar + adjective describes a state or how something is or seems at a given moment (Está cansado, La sopa está muy rica, ¡Qué guapa estás!). Some adjectives change meaning: ser listo (clever) / estar listo (ready); ser aburrido (boring) / estar aburrido (bored); ser malo (bad) / estar malo (ill, or tastes bad).
forms: ser + characteristic: Es alto. Es española. Es de madera.
estar + state: Está enfermo. Está nervioso.
ser bueno / estar bueno (tasty; also attractive – colloquial)
events: La fiesta es en mi casa. (ser for where an event takes place)

examples.es: Mi hermano es muy tranquilo, pero hoy está nervioso por el examen.
examples.en: My brother is very calm, but today he's nervous about the exam.

examples.es: La película es aburrida y yo estoy aburrida también.
examples.en: The film is boring and I'm bored too.

mastery: Chooses ser or estar in a mixed gap-fill and explains the choice
Explains the meaning change in three adjective pairs
Describes a person's character and their current mood in the same text
commonErrors: EN: uses estar for all temporary-seeming things including professions (*Está médico)
EN: *Soy aburrido meant as "I'm bored"
EN: *La fiesta está en mi casa (ser for events)
boundaries: Location is kt:es-estar-location; the rule of thumb "permanent vs temporary" has exceptions (Está muerto, Es joven) which are flagged, not drilled

primitives.binding: Same adjective (aburrido, listo, rico) with ser or estar; learner picks by intended meaning and sees how the other choice changes it
Judge sentences against the permanent/temporary rule of thumb, including counterexamples (es joven, está muerto); sort into rule and exception

kcs.label: Expressing feelings and reactions
kcs.description: Saying how you feel and reacting to news: Estoy contento/triste/preocupado/nervioso/enfadado; Tengo miedo; ¡Qué bien! ¡Qué pena! ¡Qué aburrido! ¡Increíble! ¡Uf! (relief), ¡Qué divertido!; asking: ¿Qué tal estás? ¿Cómo estás? ¿Estás bien? Expressing affection: Te quiero.

kcs.label: Physical sensations and pain: tener hambre, me duele
kcs.term: tener hambre / frío; me duele la cabeza
kcs.description: Physical sensations use tener + noun: tener hambre, sed, frío, calor, sueño, miedo (intensified with mucho/a: tengo mucha hambre). Pain uses doler like gustar: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies. Body parts take the definite article, not a possessive: Me duele la espalda.
forms: tener hambre / sed / frío / calor / sueño / miedo
me duele + singular: Me duele la cabeza.
me duelen + plural: Me duelen los ojos.
tener dolor de cabeza / de estómago
estar enfermo, estar resfriado, tener fiebre, tener tos

examples.es: Tengo mucho frío y me duele la garganta.
examples.en: I'm very cold and my throat hurts.

examples.es: ¿Qué te pasa? – Me duelen las piernas: he corrido diez kilómetros.
examples.en: What's wrong? – My legs hurt: I've run ten kilometres.

mastery: Chooses tener, estar or doler for sensations and symptoms
Uses duele/duelen and the article with body parts
Explains symptoms to a pharmacist in a role play
commonErrors: EN: *Estoy hambre / *Soy frío
EN: *Mi cabeza duele (Me duele la cabeza)
EN: *Me duele mi cabeza (article, not possessive)
EN: *muy hambre (mucha hambre)
boundaries: Other indirect-object verbs (encantar, interesar) are kt:es-encantar-interesar
Weather (hace frío) is kt:es-weather-seasons

primitives.binding: Hace frío / Tengo frío / La sopa está fría: learner matches each to weather, person or object
Pharmacy: describe symptoms, answer ¿Desde cuándo?, receive advice; branches for allergy or fever

kcs.label: Body, health and health services
kcs.term: el cuerpo, la salud y los servicios sanitarios
kcs.description: Body parts (la cabeza, la cara, los ojos, la boca, el brazo, la mano, la pierna, el pie, la espalda, el estómago, la garganta), illness and care (estar enfermo, tener gripe/fiebre/tos/alergia, tomar una pastilla/medicina), places and people (el médico, la enfermera, el hospital, el centro de salud, la farmacia, urgencias, la ambulancia) and hygiene (ducharse, lavarse los dientes, el jabón, la toalla).
forms: la cabeza, los ojos, la mano, la pierna, el pie, la espalda, el estómago
el médico, la farmacia, el centro de salud, urgencias
emergency: ¡Socorro! / llamar a una ambulancia (112 in the EU; other numbers elsewhere)

examples.es: Tengo fiebre; voy al centro de salud.
examples.en: I have a temperature; I'm going to the health centre.

examples.es: En la farmacia te dan algo para la tos.
examples.en: At the pharmacy they give you something for the cough.

mastery: Labels body parts on a picture
Understands simple instructions from a doctor or pharmacist
Explains what is wrong and asks for help in a health-centre role play
commonErrors: EN: *Tengo un frío for "I have a cold" (estoy resfriado / tengo un resfriado; constipado is a false friend)
EN: *la mano is often mistaken as masculine
boundaries: Health systems differ by country; emergency numbers must be checked locally
Pain expressions are kt:es-tener-sensations-doler

primitives.binding: Hear "Tócate la rodilla / Señala la espalda" and tap the body part on a figure
A visit to the health centre from reception to pharmacy; each step calls up the words needed, then a second visit for a different problem

kcs.label: Ir a + infinitive: plans and predictions
kcs.description: Ir (present) + a + infinitive expresses intentions and plans (Voy a estudiar medicina) and predictions from present evidence (Va a llover). It is the most frequent way to talk about the future in everyday speech, especially in Latin America.
forms: plans: El sábado vamos a ir al teatro.
prediction from evidence: Mira esas nubes: va a llover.
pronouns: Voy a llamarte / Te voy a llamar.

examples.es: ¿Qué vas a hacer este verano? – Voy a trabajar y luego voy a viajar a Perú.
examples.en: What are you going to do this summer? – I'm going to work and then travel to Peru.

examples.es: Cuidado, ¡te vas a caer!
examples.en: Careful, you're going to fall!

mastery: Forms ir a + infinitive in all persons
Distinguishes plan, intention and prediction uses
Presents their plans for next year with time expressions
commonErrors: EN: drops a: *Voy estudiar
EN: conjugates the second verb: *Voy a estudio
EN: uses the present continuous for plans as in English (*Estoy yendo a Lima mañana)
boundaries: Present for scheduled future is kt:es-present-for-future; simple future is kt:es-future-simple-recognition

primitives.binding: Timeline now → future; learner places plans (voy a…) and evidence-based predictions (va a llover) and labels each
After the model, learner writes three real plans of their own and checks which chunks transferred

kcs.label: The simple future: recognition
kcs.description: The simple future (hablaré, comerás, vivirá…) adds the endings -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án to the whole infinitive; a few verbs have short stems (tendré, haré, podré, saldré, vendré, diré, querré). At A2 learners recognise it in plans, forecasts and promises; in everyday speech ir a + infinitive is more frequent.
forms: El año que viene estudiaré ruso.
irregular stems: tendr-, har-, podr-, saldr-, vendr-, dir-
forecasts: Mañana lloverá en el norte.

examples.es: El año que viene viviré en Chile.
examples.en: Next year I'll live in Chile.

examples.es: Mañana hará sol en todo el país.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will be sunny across the country.

mastery: Recognises future forms in a weather forecast or horoscope
Converts ir a + infinitive sentences into the simple future for regular verbs
Understands promises and plans in a short email
commonErrors: EN: reads hablaré as present because of the familiar stem
EN: puts the accent in the wrong place: *hablare
boundaries: Production of irregular futures and the future of probability are B1
kcs.placementNote: PCIC lists the future (estudiaré) only as an exponent of Funciones 3.10 at A2, not in Gramática 9.1 A1-A2; it is placed here for recognition so that the function can be covered.

primitives.binding: Forecast sentences with present vs future forms (llueve / lloverá); learner decides whether it is happening now or tomorrow
A horoscope and a weather forecast; learner finds the future predictions relevant to them

kcs.label: Suggesting, inviting, accepting and declining
kcs.description: Making suggestions and invitations (¿Vamos al cine? ¿Por qué no…? ¿Qué tal si…? ¿Quedamos el viernes? Te invito a un café), confirming (Entonces, ¿vienes?), accepting with or without reservation (Vale, de acuerdo; Sí, pero más tarde), and declining politely with a reason (Lo siento, no puedo, tengo que trabajar; Otro día).
forms: Lo siento, no puedo, es que… / Otro día, ¿vale?

examples.es: ¿Qué tal si vamos a la playa el domingo? – ¡Vale! ¿A qué hora quedamos?
examples.en: How about going to the beach on Sunday? – OK! What time shall we meet?

examples.es: Te invito a cenar el viernes. – Lo siento, no puedo, es que tengo un examen. ¿Otro día?
examples.en: I'd like to take you to dinner on Friday. – Sorry, I can't, I have an exam. Another day?

mastery: Identifies acceptances, conditional acceptances and refusals in dialogues
Makes three suggestions using different structures
Arranges a meeting with a partner, declining at least one proposal politely with a reason
commonErrors: EN: refuses with a bare No sin excusa, which sounds rude
EN: *¿Quieres ir al cine conmigo? is fine but learners translate "Do you fancy…" literally
EN: doesn't realise Te invito means the speaker will pay
boundaries: Accepting/refusing simple offers at A1 is kt:es-fn-accept-refuse
Wishes (me gustaría) are kt:es-fn-wishes-me-gustaria

primitives.binding: Planning a night out: learner proposes, counter-proposes, accepts with conditions or declines with es que…; branches react to bare refusals
A guest says "Te invito" and the visitor offers to split the bill; learner explains the expectation

kcs.label: Wishes: me gustaría + infinitive
kcs.description: Me gustaría (+ infinitive) expresses wishes and polite preferences: Me gustaría vivir en el campo. ¿Te gustaría venir? It works like gustar (me/te/le/nos/os/les). Quiero is more direct; quería and me gustaría sound softer in requests.

examples.es: Me gustaría aprender a bailar salsa.
examples.en: I'd like to learn to dance salsa.

examples.es: ¿Os gustaría tener una casa más grande?
examples.en: Would you (pl.) like to have a bigger house?

mastery: Distinguishes me gusta (present liking) from me gustaría (wish)
Asks and answers about dreams and wishes
Softens a request by switching from quiero to me gustaría
commonErrors: EN: *Yo gustaría (as with gustar)
EN: *Me gustaría que ir (no que before infinitive)
boundaries: Conditional tense as a system is B1; here me gustaría is a fixed form
gustar itself is kt:es-gustar

primitives.binding: Me gusta viajar / Me gustaría viajar: learner picks by intended meaning (habit vs wish) and sees what changes
Quiero / Quería / Me gustaría in a shop, to a friend and to a teacher; learner marks the one that sounds too direct
