kcs.label: Obligation and necessity: tener que, hay que, necesitar
kcs.description: Tener que + infinitive expresses personal obligation (Tengo que trabajar); hay que + infinitive expresses general necessity with no specific subject (Hay que comprar el billete antes). No tener que / no hay que mean "not have to / no need to" (not prohibition). Necesitar + infinitive/noun and es necesario + infinitive also express need.
forms: no tienes que… = you don't have to
no hay que… = there's no need to
pronouns: Tengo que hacerlo / Lo tengo que hacer; but only Hay que hacerlo

examples.es: Mañana tengo que levantarme a las seis.
examples.en: Tomorrow I have to get up at six.

examples.es: Para entrar en el museo hay que comprar la entrada por internet.
examples.en: To get into the museum you have to buy the ticket online.

mastery: Chooses tener que or hay que by whether a specific person is meant
Explains that no tener que is not a prohibition
Lists the rules of their school or workplace with hay que / no hay que
commonErrors: EN: *Tengo trabajar (que is required)
EN: *Hay que yo… (hay que has no subject)
EN: uses no tienes que for "you mustn't" (No se puede / está prohibido)
EN: *debo for every "have to"; deber is more formal/moral
boundaries: Prohibition (está prohibido, no se puede) is kt:es-poder-permission-ability
Advice is kt:es-fn-advice-warnings

primitives.binding: Ladder from obligatory (tienes que) through advisable (es importante) to unnecessary (no hace falta / no tienes que) to prohibited (no se puede); learner places rule cards
No tienes que venir / No puedes venir: learner picks the matching picture (optional vs forbidden)

kcs.label: Poder: permission, possibility and ability
kcs.description: Poder + infinitive asks for and gives permission (¿Puedo abrir la ventana?), expresses possibility in circumstances (Hoy no puedo, tengo que trabajar) and, together with saber, ability (Puedo ayudarte). ¿Se puede? asks if one may enter or do something; responses include Sí, claro, Sí, sí, ábrela, No, lo siento, No, está prohibido.
forms: Sí, claro. / Sí, sí, ábrela. / Por supuesto.
No, lo siento. / Perdona, pero… / No, está prohibido.
saber (learned skill) vs poder (circumstances): Sé nadar, pero hoy no puedo.

examples.es: ¿Puedo cerrar la ventana? – Sí, claro, ciérrala.
examples.en: Can I close the window? – Yes, of course, close it.

examples.es: Sé conducir, pero hoy no puedo porque no tengo el carné.
examples.en: I can drive, but today I can't because I don't have my licence.

mastery: Distinguishes saber and poder in ability sentences
Asks for permission in five situations and responds to requests
Refuses permission politely with a reason
commonErrors: EN: uses poder for learned skills: *Puedo nadar (fine for circumstances, but sé nadar for skill)
EN: *¿Puedo tener…? for requests (¿Me da…? / ¿Puede darme…?)
boundaries: Requests to others (¿Puedes…?) are kt:es-fn-requests-favours
Imperative in permission answers (ábrela) is kt:es-imperative-affirmative

primitives.binding: Sé / Puedo + infinitive in contexts of skill vs circumstance; learner chooses by meaning and sees the effect of the other choice
Office situations (open window, use computer, leave early); learner asks permission and handles yes, conditional yes and refusal

levels.locator: PCIC · Funciones · Inventario A1-A2 · 4.8 · columna A2

kcs.label: Asking for things, help and favours politely
kcs.description: Requests: ¿Me das / me dejas / me pasas…? ¿Puedes + infinitive? ¿Me ayudas? ¿Puedo pedirte un favor? Indirect requests (No tengo bolígrafo = can you lend me one?). Answering: Sí, claro / Vale / Bueno, vale / Lo siento, pero no puedo. Offering help: ¿Te ayudo? ¿Necesitas algo?
forms: ¿Me das / me dejas / me pasas + noun?
Sí, claro. / Vale. / Bueno, vale. / No sé… / Lo siento, pero…
indirect: Hace frío aquí. (= close the window)

examples.es: Perdona, ¿me dejas tu bolígrafo un momento? – Sí, claro, toma.
examples.en: Sorry, can you lend me your pen for a moment? – Sure, here.

examples.es: ¿Puedes ayudarme con las maletas? – Bueno, vale, pero rápido.
examples.en: Can you help me with the suitcases? – OK, fine, but quickly.

mastery: Recognises indirect requests and responds to them
Makes requests to a friend and to a stranger with appropriate softening
Asks for and offers help in a moving-house role play
commonErrors: EN: uses the bare imperative to strangers (Dame…) without softening
EN: *¿Me puedes prestar…? is fine; but *¿Puedes prestarme a mí…? doubles the pronoun unnaturally
boundaries: Imperative forms are kt:es-imperative-affirmative
Asking for things in shops is kt:es-fn-ordering-food and kt:es-fn-shopping-prices

primitives.binding: Same request to a flatmate, a stranger and a boss; learner tunes ¿Me das…? / ¿Puedes…? / ¿Podría…? (recognition) and marks overly direct versions
Moving day: learner asks for help and favours; partner agrees, agrees with reservations or refuses; learner must respond to each

kcs.label: Giving advice and warnings
kcs.description: Simple advice: Tienes que…, Puedes…, ¿Por qué no…?, Hay que…, Es importante / necesario + infinitive, imperative (Descansa más). Warnings: ¡Cuidado! ¡Ten cuidado! Responding to advice: Sí, tienes razón; Vale, gracias.
forms: imperative (chunks here; the system follows in kt:es-imperative-affirmative): Bebe más agua.

examples.es: Estoy muy cansado. – ¿Por qué no te acuestas un rato?
examples.en: I'm very tired. – Why don't you lie down for a while?

examples.es: ¡Cuidado! El suelo está mojado.
examples.en: Careful! The floor is wet.

mastery: Matches problems with appropriate advice
Gives two pieces of advice for each of three problems using different structures
Writes a short reply to a friend asking for advice
commonErrors: EN: *Debes de… (deber de means probability; deber + infinitive for advice/obligation)
EN: *Tú deberías… is correct but is B1 (conditional); learners overuse it
boundaries: Conditional advice (deberías, yo que tú) is B1

primitives.binding: Friend describes problems (insomnia, stress, no money); learner gives advice with varied structures; repetition of the same structure is flagged
Learner writes a reply to an advice-column letter, compares with a model, rewrites one piece of advice

levels.locator: PCIC · Funciones · Inventario A1-A2 · 4.18 · columna A2

kcs.label: Affirmative imperative (tú, vosotros, usted, ustedes)
kcs.description: Tú imperative = 3rd person singular present (habla, come, escribe, cierra); irregular short forms: di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ven, ve, sé. Vosotros: infinitive -r → -d (hablad, comed). Usted/ustedes take the present subjunctive forms (hable, coma; hablen, coman), learned here as fixed forms. Pronouns attach to the end and may need an accent: cómpralo, siéntate, dale.
forms: tú: habla, come, escribe; cierra, vuelve, pide (stem change)
irregular tú: di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ven, ve
usted / ustedes: hable / hablen, coma / coman, siga / sigan
vos imperative (hablá, comé, vení) recognised only

examples.es: Abre la ventana, por favor, y pon la mesa.
examples.en: Open the window, please, and set the table.

examples.es: Siga todo recto y gire la segunda a la derecha.
examples.en: Go straight on and take the second on the right. (usted)

mastery: Forms tú imperatives of regular, stem-changing and irregular verbs
Converts tú instructions to usted for a formal context
Writes a simple recipe or set of instructions with at least eight imperatives
commonErrors: EN: uses the infinitive as imperative in speech (*Abrir la puerta) – it occurs on signs but not to a person
EN: *hace for haz, *pone for pon
EN: forgets the accent when adding pronouns: *comprala
boundaries: Negative imperatives (no hables) need the subjunctive and are B1
Pronoun attachment in general is kt:es-clitic-position

primitives.binding: Learner derives tú imperative = él/ella present, then applies to unseen verbs; irregular eight are flagged; usted forms shown as a second set
Recipe pictures out of order; learner orders them and writes one imperative per step

kcs.label: Giving and following detailed directions
kcs.description: Step-by-step directions with imperatives and sequence: Sigue todo recto, cruza la plaza, gira / dobla a la izquierda, coge / toma la tercera calle, sube / baja la escalera; landmarks with encima/debajo, delante/detrás, enfrente de, al final de; distance (Está a 200 metros) and estimates (Hay unos diez minutos andando).
forms: gira / gire, dobla (Latin America) a la derecha
cruza / cruce la calle, el puente
enfrente de, delante de, detrás de, al final de, en la esquina

examples.es: Sal de la estación, cruza la plaza y toma la primera calle a la izquierda. El hotel está enfrente del banco.
examples.en: Leave the station, cross the square and take the first street on the left. The hotel is opposite the bank.

examples.es: Para ir a la cafetería, baje las escaleras y siga por el pasillo.
examples.en: To get to the cafeteria, go down the stairs and continue along the corridor.

mastery: Follows a multi-step route on a map
Gives directions to a visitor using tú or usted consistently
Writes directions to their home for a guest
commonErrors: EN: mixes tú and usted imperatives in one set of directions
EN: *gira en la izquierda (a la izquierda)
boundaries: Basic A1 directions are kt:es-fn-directions-basic; the imperative system is kt:es-imperative-affirmative

primitives.binding: Detailed directions in a 3D-style street plan; learner traces the route; the final position is the evidence
Each partner has a map with different destinations; they must give and follow directions to swap locations

kcs.label: Getting attention and addressing people
kcs.description: Formulaic imperatives that open an exchange: Perdona / Perdone (excuse me), Oye / Oiga (hey / excuse me), Mira / Mire (look), Disculpa / Disculpe. Choose the tú or usted form. Answering the phone: ¿Diga? / ¿Dígame? (Spain), ¿Aló? (much of Latin America), ¿Bueno? (Mexico), ¿Sí?

examples.es: Oiga, perdone, ¿sabe dónde hay una farmacia?
examples.en: Excuse me, do you know where there's a pharmacy?

examples.es: Mira, este es mi hermano Pablo.
examples.en: Look, this is my brother Pablo.

mastery: Chooses the tú or usted attention-getter for a given addressee
Recognises phone-answering formulas from different countries
Opens three street encounters politely
commonErrors: EN: uses Oye to strangers older than them (Oiga / Perdone)
EN: thinks Oiga sounds rude; in Spain it is a normal attention-getter, though perdone is softer
boundaries: Telephone calls in full are kt:es-fn-telephone

primitives.binding: Same request to a child, a police officer and a waiter; learner picks oye/oiga, perdona/perdone and marks the mismatch
Phone-answering formulas by country; learner predicts who is answering from where

levels.locator: PCIC · Funciones · Inventario A1-A2 · 5.3 · columna A2

kcs.label: Llevar and traer: taking and bringing
kcs.description: Traer = bring towards the place where the speaker is (or will be); llevar = take away from it, or to another place. ¿Me traes un vaso de agua? (here) vs Llevo los niños al colegio (there). Llevar also means wear and carry. Like ir/venir, the choice depends on the speaker's location, not the listener's.
forms: traer: hacia aquí: Tráeme el libro.
llevar: hacia allí: Lleva esto a la oficina.
ir/venir parallel: venir + traer (here), ir + llevar (there)

examples.es: ¿Nos puede traer más pan, por favor?
examples.en: Could you bring us more bread, please?

examples.es: Mañana llevo el postre a casa de mis padres.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm taking dessert to my parents' house.

mastery: Chooses llevar or traer from the speaker's position in pictures
Uses traer in restaurant requests
Explains what they will take to a party at a friend's house
commonErrors: EN: follows English bring/take when talking to the listener's place: *Te traigo el libro mañana a tu casa (usually te llevo…, though usage varies)
EN: *trayo for traigo
boundaries: Regional usage of traer/llevar towards the listener varies; this KC teaches the speaker-centred core

primitives.binding: Scenes with speaker location marked; learner moves objects and chooses traer/llevar; changing the speaker position flips the answer
Sentences where only llevar/traer tells whether the object ends up with the speaker

levels.locator: PCIC · Tácticas y estrategias pragmáticas · Inventario A1-A2 · 1.3 · columna A2

kcs.label: Direct object pronouns: lo, la, los, las
kcs.term: pronombres de objeto directo: me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las
kcs.description: Direct object pronouns replace a noun that receives the action: me, te, lo/la, nos, os, los/las. Lo/la/los/las agree with the noun they replace (¿El pan? Lo compro yo. ¿Las llaves? No las encuentro). When the object is placed first for emphasis or topic, the pronoun is repeated: El café lo tomo solo. Lo can also refer to a whole idea: No lo sé.
forms: me, te, lo / la, nos, os, los / las
before the conjugated verb: Lo veo. No la conozco.
agreement with the replaced noun: las gafas → las
topic first + pronoun: Los deberes los hago por la noche.
neuter lo: No lo sé. / Ya lo sé.
variation: le for a male person (leísmo, accepted in Spain: Le vi ayer); Latin America and most of Spain's written norm use lo

examples.es: ¿Dónde está mi móvil? – No sé, no lo veo.
examples.en: Where's my phone? – I don't know, I can't see it.

examples.es: Las fotos las tengo en el ordenador.
examples.en: I have the photos on the computer.

mastery: Replaces object nouns with the correct pronoun in gender and number
Answers questions without repeating the noun
Uses the topic + pronoun order to talk about chores (La compra la hago yo)
commonErrors: EN: omits the pronoun: *¿El libro? Sí, tengo.
EN: puts the pronoun after the conjugated verb: *Veo lo
EN: uses lo for feminine nouns: *¿La película? Lo vi.
ZH: omits objects freely as in Chinese (*¿Compraste el pan? – Sí, compré.)
boundaries: Leísmo: using le for a male person as direct object (Le vi) is accepted for masculine singular persons in Spain; learners should recognise it and may use lo everywhere. Laísmo (La dije) is non-standard and is not taught
Indirect objects are kt:es-indirect-object-pronouns; positions with infinitives and imperatives are kt:es-clitic-position

primitives.binding: Short dialogues; learner links each lo/la/los/las to the noun it replaces and fixes mismatches in gender or number
Pronoun cards placed before the conjugated verb; learner drags them into position and reads the result aloud

levels.locator: PCIC · Gramática · Inventario A1-A2 · 7.1 · columna A2

kcs.label: Personal a before human direct objects
kcs.description: When the direct object is a specific person (or a pet treated like one), it is introduced by a: Veo a María. Conozco a tu hermano. Busco a mi hijo. There is no a with things (Veo la casa) or usually with unspecific people (Busco un médico / Necesito un profesor). Al = a + el.
forms: verb + a + specific person: Llamo a mi madre.
a + el = al: Veo al profesor.
no a with things: Busco mis llaves.
unspecific: Busco un camarero (any) vs Busco al camarero (the one I know)
with tener usually no a: Tengo dos hermanos.

examples.es: Esta tarde visito a mis abuelos.
examples.en: This afternoon I'm visiting my grandparents.

examples.es: ¿Conoces a Lucía? – Sí, la conozco del trabajo.
examples.en: Do you know Lucía? – Yes, I know her from work.

mastery: Inserts or omits a before direct objects in mixed sentences
Asks ¿A quién…? questions
Describes who they visit, call and help in a week
commonErrors: EN: omits a with people: *Veo mi hermano
EN: adds a with things: *Busco a mi libro
EN: confuses personal a with the preposition of direction
boundaries: Variation with animals and organisations is left for later; tener + a for specific people (Tengo a mi madre enferma) is B1

primitives.binding: Sentences with person and thing objects; learner marks who receives the action and decides whether a is needed
English "I see Maria" vs Spanish Veo a María: learner aligns the parts and spots the extra word

levels.locator: PCIC · Gramática · Inventario A1-A2 · 7.1 · columna A2

kcs.label: Indirect object pronouns: le, les (se)
kcs.term: pronombres de objeto indirecto: me, te, le, nos, os, les
kcs.description: Indirect object pronouns mark the person who receives or benefits: me, te, le, nos, os, les. Le/les are often doubled by a phrase with a: Le doy el libro a Juan. When le/les meets lo/la/los/las, le/les becomes se: Se lo doy (not *le lo). At A2, se lo is learned as a chunk.
forms: me, te, le, nos, os, les
verbs: dar, decir, escribir, regalar, preguntar, mandar, explicar
doubling: Le escribo a mi abuela.
order: indirect + direct: Me lo das. Te la doy.
le/les + lo/la → se lo / se la: Se lo explico.
usted: Le llamo mañana (Spain, leísmo de cortesía) / Lo llamo (LatAm)

examples.es: Le he regalado un libro a mi padre.
examples.en: I've given my father a book.

examples.es: ¿Me dejas tu coche? – Sí, te lo dejo, pero tráemelo mañana.
examples.en: Will you lend me your car? – Yes, I'll lend it to you, but bring it back tomorrow.

mastery: Chooses direct or indirect pronouns for the verb
Combines two pronouns in the right order including se lo
Tells who they give presents to and what, without repeating nouns
commonErrors: EN: *Le lo doy (se lo)
EN: drops the doubling pronoun: *Doy el libro a Juan is acceptable, but *A Juan doy el libro is not
EN: uses lo/la for the recipient: *La escribo a mi madre
boundaries: Variation: in Spain le is common for usted as direct object (Le acompaño); in Latin America lo/la. Both are taught for recognition
Gustar-type verbs are kt:es-gustar and kt:es-encantar-interesar

primitives.binding: Event pictures (giving, telling, sending); learner identifies giver, thing and receiver and picks the pronoun for each
Unpack se lo doy into "le + lo" and "to him/her + it", then pack new pairs

levels.locator: PCIC · Gramática · Inventario A1-A2 · 7.1 · columna A2

kcs.label: Where pronouns go: before the verb or attached
kcs.description: Unstressed pronouns go before a conjugated verb (Lo compro) but are attached to the end of an affirmative imperative (Cómpralo), an infinitive (Voy a comprarlo) or a gerund (Estoy comprándolo). With a conjugated verb + infinitive or gerund both positions are possible: Lo voy a comprar / Voy a comprarlo. Attaching may require a written accent.
forms: conjugated verb: Te llamo. No lo sé.
infinitive: Quiero verte. Hay que hacerlo.
two positions: Te voy a llamar / Voy a llamarte
reflexive + object: Me lo pongo / Póntelo
accent when stress shifts: compra → cómpralo

examples.es: ¿La película? Quiero verla esta noche. / La quiero ver esta noche.
examples.en: The film? I want to see it tonight.

examples.es: Este jersey es bonito. ¡Pruébatelo!
examples.en: This sweater is nice. Try it on!

mastery: Places pronouns correctly with conjugated verbs, imperatives, infinitives and gerunds
Transforms between the two possible positions
Adds the accent when attaching pronouns
commonErrors: EN: places after the conjugated verb: *Quiero la ver / *Veo la
EN: splits the cluster: *Lo quiero comprarlo (doubled)
EN: forgets the accent: *pruebatelo
boundaries: Negative imperatives with pronouns before the verb (No lo compres) are B1

primitives.binding: Pronoun and verb cards; learner chooses before or after-attached for each verb form and sees where the accent must be added
Build sentences from me, lo, voy a, dar in both legal orders; illegal orders are rejected with the rule shown

kcs.label: Verbs like gustar: encantar, interesar, importar, molestar, parecer
kcs.description: Encantar (love), interesar, importar, molestar, apetecer (Spain), quedar (fit/suit) and parecer work like gustar: the thing liked is the subject and agrees with the verb; the person is an indirect object. Me encantan los perros. ¿Te interesa la historia? ¿Qué te parece el piso? Interest and dislike can be graded: Me interesa mucho / No me interesa nada / Odio…
forms: Me encanta + infinitive: Me encanta bailar.
¿Qué te parece…? – Me parece muy bonito.
A mí me encanta… ¿Y a ti? – A mí también / A mí no.
no me interesa nada / odio / no soporto

examples.es: Me encantan las novelas policiacas, pero no me interesa la poesía.
examples.en: I love crime novels, but I'm not interested in poetry.

examples.es: ¿Qué te parece este restaurante? – Me parece un poco caro.
examples.en: What do you think of this restaurant? – It seems a bit expensive to me.

mastery: Makes the verb agree with the thing liked (encanta / encantan)
Uses a mí también / a mí tampoco correctly in replies
Talks about interests and dislikes in a short interview
commonErrors: EN: *Me encanto la música / *Yo encanto la música
EN: *Me encanta mucho (encantar is already strong)
EN: *Me interesa en el arte
boundaries: gustar itself is kt:es-gustar; preferences are kt:es-fn-preferences

primitives.binding: Learner transfers the gustar pattern (thing = subject) to encantar, interesar, molestar and checks agreement with plural things
Interest survey: learner asks ¿Te interesa…? and reports A Ana le encanta…, a Tom no le interesa nada…

kcs.label: Pronouns after prepositions: para mí, contigo
kcs.description: After prepositions, Spanish uses mí, ti and the subject forms for the rest: para mí, para ti, con él, sin nosotros, de ellos. With con the forms are conmigo and contigo. After entre and según, yo and tú are used: entre tú y yo. A mí, a ti… double indirect objects for emphasis or contrast: A mí me gusta, ¿y a ti?
forms: mí, ti, él, ella, usted, nosotros/as, vosotros/as, ellos/as, ustedes
entre tú y yo; según tú
a mí me…, a ti te… (emphasis)

examples.es: Este regalo es para ti. ¿Vienes conmigo a la fiesta?
examples.en: This present is for you. Are you coming to the party with me?

examples.es: A mí no me gusta el fútbol, pero a él le encanta.
examples.en: I don't like football, but he loves it.

mastery: Uses mí/ti and conmigo/contigo after prepositions
Writes mí with an accent and mi without
Uses a mí / a ti for contrast in conversation
commonErrors: EN: *con mí / *con ti
EN: *para yo / *para me
EN: *mi without accent for the pronoun
boundaries: Reflexive sí / consigo is B1

primitives.binding: Para mí / para mi madre: learner decides whether mi/mí is a pronoun or possessive from the following word
Preposition + person prompts (con + yo, para + tú); learner types the form before it is revealed

kcs.label: The present perfect (pretérito perfecto compuesto)
kcs.description: Present of haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + past participle (-ado/-ido). Irregular participles: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto, muerto. Uses: experiences in life (¿Has estado en México?) and events in a time period that includes now (Hoy he trabajado mucho; Esta semana he ido al cine). In much of Latin America and in parts of Spain the simple preterite is preferred for today's events (Hoy trabajé mucho).
forms: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + participle
hablar → hablado, comer → comido, vivir → vivido
irregular: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto
time markers: hoy, esta mañana, este año, alguna vez, nunca, ya, todavía no
participle does not change: Ellas han salido.
pronouns before haber: Lo he visto.

examples.es: ¿Has estado alguna vez en Cuba? – No, nunca he estado allí.
examples.en: Have you ever been to Cuba? – No, I've never been there.

examples.es: Esta mañana he desayunado muy poco.
examples.en: I had very little breakfast this morning.

mastery: Forms the present perfect of regular and the eight most frequent irregular participles
Talks about life experiences with alguna vez / nunca
Recounts what they have done today
commonErrors: EN: *He visitado Barcelona en 2019 (past date needs preterite)
EN: uses tener as auxiliary: *Tengo comido
EN: splits haber and participle: *He ya comido
EN: makes the participle agree: *Ellas han salidas
boundaries: Regional variation: Latin American Spanish and some Peninsular regions use the preterite for recent events; both are correct in their variety
Contrast with the preterite is kt:es-perfecto-vs-indefinido

primitives.binding: Timeline with a bracket "today / this week / my life"; learner places events inside the bracket with he + participle
Participle rule -ado/-ido derived from examples, then applied; irregulars collected as exceptions

kcs.label: Ya, todavía no, aún no: things done and still to do
kcs.description: Ya (already) and todavía no / aún no (not yet) mark whether an expected event has happened: ¿Ya has comprado los billetes? – Sí, ya los he comprado / No, todavía no. Ya and todavía no go before haber or at the end, never between haber and the participle. Todavía + affirmative = still: Todavía vive con sus padres.
forms: todavía no / aún no + he… + participle
short answers: Sí, ya. / No, todavía no.
ya no = not any more: Ya no fumo.

examples.es: ¿Ya has hecho los deberes? – No, todavía no.
examples.en: Have you done your homework yet? – No, not yet.

examples.es: Ya no vivo en Sevilla, pero todavía tengo amigos allí.
examples.en: I don't live in Seville any more, but I still have friends there.

mastery: Ticks off a to-do list with ya / todavía no
Distinguishes todavía (still) from ya no (not any more)
Asks and answers about trip preparations
commonErrors: EN: *He ya comido (position)
EN: confuses ya no and todavía no
EN: *No todavía (todavía no)
boundaries: Ya in the preterite (Ya terminé) is common in Latin America; recognised here

primitives.binding: Preparing for a trip: a checklist scene; learner reports what is done and not done, then a second list (moving house) with no hints
Expected-event marker on a timeline; learner places ya, todavía no, ya no and todavía

kcs.label: Starting, finishing and repeating: empezar a, acabar de, volver a, dejar de
kcs.description: Verbal periphrases express phases of an action: empezar / comenzar a + infinitive (begin), terminar de + infinitive (finish), acabar de + infinitive (have just done), volver a + infinitive (do again), dejar de + infinitive (stop doing), seguir + gerund (keep doing).
forms: empezar a + infinitive: Empiezo a trabajar a las nueve.
acabar de + infinitive = have just: Acabo de llegar.
volver a + infinitive = again: Vuelve a llover.
dejar de + infinitive = stop: He dejado de fumar.
seguir + gerund = keep / still: Sigue lloviendo.

examples.es: Acabo de llegar a casa y ya empieza a llover.
examples.en: I've just got home and it's already starting to rain.

examples.es: Mi padre ha dejado de fumar, pero vuelve a comer dulces.
examples.en: My father has stopped smoking, but he's eating sweets again.

mastery: Matches each periphrasis to its phase on a timeline
Uses the right preposition (a / de) with each
Talks about habits they have started, stopped or restarted
commonErrors: EN: *Acabo llegar / *Empiezo trabajar (missing preposition)
EN: uses again instead of volver a: *Llueve otra vez is fine, but learners avoid volver a
EN: *Dejo de trabajar meaning "I leave work"
boundaries: estar + gerund is kt:es-estar-gerund; ir a + infinitive is kt:es-ir-a-infinitive

primitives.binding: Action bar with start, middle, end and restart; learner attaches each periphrasis to its phase
Acabo de comer / Termino de comer / Dejo de comer: learner chooses the picture each describes

kcs.label: The preterite (pretérito indefinido): regular verbs
kcs.description: The simple preterite expresses completed events at a finished past time (ayer, el año pasado, en 2010). Endings: -ar: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron; -er/-ir: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. Stress on the ending matters: hablo (I speak) vs habló (he spoke). The nosotros form of -ar and -ir verbs is the same as the present (hablamos, vivimos).
forms: -ar: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron
-er/-ir: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron
ayer, anoche, el lunes pasado, la semana pasada, hace dos años, en 2015

examples.es: Ayer cené con unos amigos y volví a casa a las doce.
examples.en: Yesterday I had dinner with some friends and got home at twelve.

examples.es: Mis abuelos vivieron en Argentina diez años.
examples.en: My grandparents lived in Argentina for ten years.

mastery: Forms the preterite of regular verbs in all persons
Hears and reads the stress difference between hablo and habló
Writes what they did last weekend
commonErrors: EN: forgets the accent: *hablo for habló
EN: *comistes (vos/colloquial) for comiste
EN: uses the perfect with past dates: *Ayer he visto
boundaries: Spelling changes (busqué, llegué) are kt:es-orth-spelling-a2
Contrast with the present perfect is kt:es-perfecto-vs-indefinido

primitives.binding: Learner builds the two ending sets from hablar and comer, then conjugates unseen verbs; nosotros overlap with the present is pointed out
Pairs hablo / habló, trabajo / trabajó; learner identifies who and when from stress alone

kcs.label: Frequent irregular preterites
kcs.description: The most frequent verbs have irregular preterites with a special stem and unstressed endings (-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron): estar → estuve, tener → tuve, poder → pude, poner → puse, hacer → hice (hizo), venir → vine, querer → quise, saber → supe, decir → dije (dijeron), traer → traje. Ser and ir share fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Dar → di, ver → vi. -ir stem changers change in 3rd person: pidió, durmió.
forms: estuve, tuve, pude, puse, supe (-u- stems)
ser / ir: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron

examples.es: El verano pasado fuimos a México y estuvimos tres semanas.
examples.en: Last summer we went to Mexico and stayed three weeks.

examples.es: ¿Qué hiciste el sábado? – Tuve que trabajar.
examples.en: What did you do on Saturday? – I had to work.

mastery: Supplies the preterite of 15 frequent irregular verbs
Distinguishes fue = was/went from context
Narrates a trip using at least six irregular preterites
commonErrors: EN: regularises: *estué, *hací, *tení
EN: adds accents to irregular forms: *estuvé, *hizó
EN: *dijieron / *trajieron
boundaries: Less frequent irregulars (conducir → conduje, caber) are B1

primitives.binding: Infinitive + person prompts; learner types the irregular preterite before reveal; spaced re-appearance of missed items
Stem groups (-u-, -i-, -j-) with shared endings; learner predicts unseen members of each group

kcs.label: Past time expressions and dates
kcs.description: Locating events in the past: ayer, anteayer, anoche, el lunes / mes / año pasado, la semana pasada, hace + period (hace tres días), en + year or month, el + date (el 12 de octubre de 1492), de pequeño/a, cuando era niño (imperfect, recognition), al día siguiente, después, luego.
forms: el año pasado / la semana pasada
al día siguiente / dos días después

examples.es: Me mudé a Madrid hace cinco años, en 2020.
examples.en: I moved to Madrid five years ago, in 2020.

examples.es: Anoche llegamos tarde y al día siguiente dormimos hasta las once.
examples.en: Last night we arrived late and the next day we slept until eleven.

mastery: Places events on a timeline from time expressions
Converts dates into hace + period and back
Writes a short timeline of their life
commonErrors: EN: *hace dos años atrás (redundant)
EN: *dos años hace
EN: *en el lunes pasado (no en)
boundaries: hace + period with present (Vivo aquí desde hace…) is kt:es-duration-desde-hace

Years and dates read aloud (mil novecientos noventa y nueve); learner writes the number and the hace equivalent

kcs.label: Present perfect or preterite?
kcs.description: In standard Peninsular use, the present perfect is used with time frames that include now (hoy, este año, alguna vez, nunca) and the preterite with finished times (ayer, en 2010, el verano pasado). In most of Latin America (and Canarias, Galicia, Asturias) the preterite covers most completed events, even today's, and the perfect is reserved for experiences or continuing situations. Learners should be consistent within one variety.
forms: perfect: hoy, esta mañana, esta semana, este año, alguna vez, nunca, ya, todavía no
preterite: ayer, anoche, el año pasado, en 2010, hace + time
Spain: Hoy he comido paella. Ayer comí pescado.
Mexico/Argentina: Hoy comí paella. Ayer comí pescado.
experience question in both: ¿Has estado alguna vez en…? / ¿Estuviste alguna vez en…?

examples.es: Este año he viajado mucho: en marzo fui a Lima y en julio a Quito.
examples.en: This year I've travelled a lot: in March I went to Lima and in July to Quito.

examples.es: ¿Has visto la última película de Almodóvar? – Sí, la vi ayer.
examples.en: Have you seen Almodóvar's latest film? – Yes, I saw it yesterday.

mastery: Chooses perfect or preterite from the time marker in a Peninsular text
Recognises the Latin American preterite for recent events as correct
Writes a summary of their year mixing both tenses appropriately
commonErrors: EN: follows English: *Ayer he comido for "I ate yesterday"
EN: *En 2015 he estado en Perú
EN: assumes Latin American Hoy comí is wrong
boundaries: The perfect for recent events is a regional norm, not a universal rule; tests should declare the variety they assume

primitives.binding: Same day narrated by a speaker from Madrid and one from Mexico City; learner notes where the tenses differ and states the regional norm
Timeline with "now-including" bracket vs finished periods; learner sorts time markers and then events

kcs.label: Spelling changes in verb forms and word families
kcs.description: To keep the same consonant sound, some verb forms change their spelling: c → qu before e (buscar → busqué), g → gu before e (llegar → llegué, pagar → pagué), z → c before e (empezar → empecé), and unstressed i between vowels → y (leer → leyó, oír → oyeron). The same rules explain plurals like lápiz → lápices and spellings like coger → cojo, seguir → sigo.
forms: z → c: empecé, crucé; lápiz → lápices, vez → veces
i → y: leyó, leyeron, oyó, construyó
g → j: coger → cojo, elegir → elijo

examples.es: Ayer llegué tarde porque busqué aparcamiento durante media hora.
examples.en: Yesterday I arrived late because I looked for parking for half an hour.

examples.es: Empecé el libro el lunes y lo leyó también mi hermana.
examples.en: I started the book on Monday and my sister read it too.

mastery: Spells the yo preterite of -car, -gar, -zar verbs correctly
Explains why the spelling changes (same sound)
Writes plurals of words ending in -z
commonErrors: EN: *buscé, *llegé, *empezé
EN: *leió, *oieron
EN: *lápizes
boundaries: Basic sound-spelling correspondences are kt:es-orth-sound-spelling

kcs.label: The imperfect: habits and descriptions in the past
kcs.description: The imperfect describes past habits (De niño jugaba al fútbol), what people, places and situations were like (La casa era grande) and the background to an event (Llovía cuando salí). Regular endings: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban; -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Only three irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía).
forms: -ar: hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban
ser: era…; ir: iba…; ver: veía…
habit: Antes / De pequeño / Cuando era niño + imperfect
background + event: Estaba en casa cuando sonó el teléfono.

examples.es: Cuando era pequeña, vivía en un pueblo y iba al colegio andando.
examples.en: When I was little, I lived in a village and walked to school.

examples.es: Hacía mucho frío y no había nadie en la calle.
examples.en: It was very cold and there was nobody in the street.

mastery: Forms the imperfect of regular verbs and ser, ir, ver
Describes childhood habits with antes / de pequeño
Chooses imperfect for background and preterite for events in a short story
commonErrors: EN: uses the preterite for habits: *De niño jugué al fútbol todos los días
EN: translates "used to" with soler only or *usaba
EN: *éramos for era, *iba for veía (irregular confusion)
boundaries: The full preterite/imperfect contrast in complex narration is B1; here background vs event in simple stories

primitives.binding: Story timeline with a shaded background band and event points; learner tags each verb as band (imperfect) or point (preterite)
Then-and-now pictures of a town; learner describes the old picture in the imperfect

kcs.label: Ordering events: primero, después, luego, al final
kcs.description: Connectors order steps and events: primero, después (de), luego, más tarde, entonces, al final / por último, finalmente; antes de / después de + infinitive. Primero/segundo can order points in a talk. Enumeration: por un lado… por otro.

examples.es: Primero desayuné, luego fui al banco y al final comí con mi hermana.
examples.en: First I had breakfast, then I went to the bank and finally I had lunch with my sister.

examples.es: Antes de salir, cierra las ventanas.
examples.en: Before leaving, close the windows.

mastery: Orders jumbled sentences using connectors
Uses at least four different connectors in a narrative
Uses antes de / después de + infinitive
commonErrors: EN: *después que comer (después de comer)
EN: overuses y entonces in every sentence
boundaries: Causal connectors are kt:es-por-eso-entonces; reference across sentences is kt:es-disc-reference-ellipsis

A short story with connectors highlighted; learner draws the order of events and adds a missing connector

kcs.label: Telling a simple story or anecdote
kcs.description: Telling a short story about a past experience in order: opening the topic (¿Sabes qué me pasó ayer?), setting the scene (imperfect), events (preterite), reaction and ending (Y al final…, Total, que…). Listeners invite and react: ¿Qué pasó? ¿Y entonces? ¡No me digas! Written forms: a postcard, a diary entry, a short biography.
forms: opening: ¿Sabes qué me pasó? / Te cuento…
setting: Era sábado y hacía sol…
reactions: ¡No me digas! ¿Y qué hiciste? ¡Qué susto!
closing: Al final… / Y eso es todo.
biography: Nació en…, Estudió…, Murió en…

examples.es: ¿Sabes qué me pasó ayer? Estaba en el metro y de repente vi a mi profesor de primaria.
examples.en: Do you know what happened to me yesterday? I was on the metro and suddenly I saw my primary-school teacher.

examples.es: Frida Kahlo nació en 1907 en Coyoacán y empezó a pintar después de un accidente.
examples.en: Frida Kahlo was born in 1907 in Coyoacán and started painting after an accident.

mastery: Tells a 6–10 sentence anecdote with opening, events and ending
Reacts to a partner's story with at least three reactions
Writes a short biography from notes
commonErrors: EN: tells events in the present without marking past
EN: no opening or closing, story stops abruptly
EN: *¿Y después qué pasado?
boundaries: Long or formal narratives are B1; written narrative genres per PCIC are A2 reception and production at short length

primitives.binding: Comic strip of an incident; learner tells it with background, events and ending; missing parts are flagged
Learner starts with three events, then adds setting, reactions and an ending in successive passes
Listener role: learner reacts and asks ¿Y entonces? at the right moments in a recorded anecdote

kcs.label: Describing objects: shape, material, condition and identifying one
kcs.description: Describing things by shape (redondo, cuadrado, largo), size, material (de madera, de plástico, de algodón), consistency (duro, blando), condition (nuevo, viejo, roto, limpio, sucio), origin (es de China, viene de…) and use (sirve para…). Identifying one among several: el de la izquierda, la roja, el que está en la mesa, este no, ese.
forms: es de madera / de metal / de plástico / de algodón
está roto / limpio / sucio; es nuevo / viejo
sirve para + infinitive / se usa para…
el / la / los / las de + phrase: el de cuero
el / la + adjective: la grande, el azul
el que + clause: el que lleva gafas

examples.es: ¿Cuál es tu maleta? – La negra, la de ruedas.
examples.en: Which is your suitcase? – The black one, the one with wheels.

examples.es: Es una cosa pequeña, de plástico, que sirve para abrir botellas.
examples.en: It's a small plastic thing that's used for opening bottles.

mastery: Describes an object so that a partner can identify it
Identifies one item among several with el de / el + adjective / el que
Describes a lost item at a lost-property office
commonErrors: EN: *la una negra (la negra)
EN: *hecho de madera overused; es de madera is normal
EN: *el uno que… for "the one that"
boundaries: Comparisons are kt:es-comparatives; relative que in general is kt:es-relative-que

primitives.binding: Learner describes one of several similar objects; partner must pick it; success depends on contrasting features
Lost-property scene; learner describes their item by shape, colour, material and condition; checklist of features

kcs.label: Comparing: más/menos… que, tan… como, mejor, peor
kcs.description: Comparisons of adjectives, adverbs and nouns: más / menos + adjective + que (más caro que), tan + adjective/adverb + como (tan alto como), tanto/a/os/as + noun + como (tantos libros como), verb + más / menos / tanto como. Irregular: mejor, peor, mayor (older), menor (younger). With numbers: más de (más de cien). Degree: un poco más, mucho más, bastante.

examples.es: Este piso es más pequeño que el otro, pero es mucho más barato.
examples.en: This flat is smaller than the other one, but it's much cheaper.

examples.es: Mi hermano es mayor que yo, pero no es tan alto como yo.
examples.en: My brother is older than me, but he isn't as tall as me.

mastery: Forms the four types of comparison
Uses mejor / peor and mayor / menor instead of *más bueno / *más viejo where expected
Compares two flats or two cities in a short text
commonErrors: EN: *más bueno for "better" (mejor; más bueno exists for character in colloquial speech)
EN: *tan como + noun (tanto como)
EN: *más que cien (más de cien)
EN: *más alto de mí
boundaries: The superlative (el más caro de) and -ísimo are recognised only at A2; PCIC A1-A2 Gramática 2.5 lists comparatives

primitives.binding: Two products on a scale of price, size and quality; learner states each relation with más/menos/tan

kcs.label: Exclamations and evaluations: ¡Qué bonito!, ¡Qué + noun + tan…!
kcs.description: ¡Qué + adjective! (¡Qué bonito!), ¡Qué + adverb! (¡Qué bien!), ¡Qué + noun! (¡Qué calor!, ¡Qué suerte!) and ¡Qué + noun + tan/más + adjective! (¡Qué casa tan grande!) express surprise and evaluation. ¡Cuánto + noun! (¡Cuánta gente!) for quantity. General evaluation: Es estupendo / horrible / genial / fatal; Está muy bien / regular / mal.
forms: Es genial / estupendo / horrible; Está fatal

examples.es: ¡Qué vista tan bonita! ¡Y qué tranquilo es este pueblo!
examples.en: What a beautiful view! And how quiet this village is!

examples.es: ¡Cuánta gente hay hoy en la playa!

mastery: Reacts to pictures and news with appropriate exclamations
Forms ¡Qué + noun + tan + adjective! with agreement
Writes accent marks on exclamative qué and cuánto
commonErrors: EN: *¡Qué una casa bonita! (no article)
EN: *¡Cómo bonito! (¡Qué bonito!)
EN: forgets the accent: *¡Que bonito!
boundaries: Exclamations as reactions to feelings are kt:es-fn-feelings; superlative -ísimo is recognised only

primitives.binding: Holiday photos; learner reacts with a different exclamation pattern to each and gets feedback on agreement
Build ¡Qué + noun + tan + adjective! from cards; illegal orders (*¡Qué tan casa!) rejected

kcs.label: Adverbs in -mente
kcs.description: Many manner adverbs are formed from the feminine singular adjective + -mente: rápido → rápidamente, tranquilo → tranquilamente, fácil → fácilmente. The adjective keeps its written accent (fácilmente). In everyday speech many speakers use bien, mal, rápido, despacio instead. Frequent: normalmente, generalmente, realmente, especialmente, solamente, perfectamente.
forms: alternative: hablar rápido / despacio / bien / mal

examples.es: Habla despacio, por favor: no entiendo perfectamente.
examples.en: Speak slowly, please: I don't understand perfectly.

examples.es: Normalmente llego puntual, pero hoy he venido tranquilamente.
examples.en: I normally arrive on time, but today I came along at a leisurely pace.

mastery: Forms -mente adverbs from adjectives of both types
Keeps the adjective's accent
Describes how people do things in a picture

EN: drops the accent: *facilmente
EN: *buenamente for well (bien)
boundaries: Coordinated -mente adverbs (lenta y claramente) are B1

kcs.label: Stressed possessives: mío, tuyo, suyo
kcs.description: Stressed possessives (mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro, vuestro, suyo) agree with the thing owned and appear after ser (Es mío), after a noun (un amigo mío), or with an article as a pronoun (el mío, la tuya). They replace de + pronoun for first and second person: *la casa de mí → la casa mía / mi casa. Apposition is also covered: mi hermano Juan, la calle Alcalá.
forms: mío/a/os/as, tuyo, suyo, nuestro, vuestro, suyo
ser + possessive: ¿Es tuyo? – Sí, es mío.
article + possessive: el mío, las tuyas
mi casa / la casa mía (not *la casa de mí)
apposition: mi amiga Lucía, el museo Picasso

examples.es: ¿De quién es esta chaqueta? – Es mía.
examples.en: Whose jacket is this? – It's mine.

examples.es: Mi coche es rojo; el tuyo es azul, ¿no?
examples.en: My car is red; yours is blue, isn't it?

mastery: Answers ¿De quién es…? with stressed possessives
Uses el mío / la tuya to avoid repeating nouns
Distinguishes mi (before noun) from mío (after or alone)
commonErrors: EN: *Es mi / *Es la mía casa
EN: *un amigo de mí
EN: no agreement: *las mío
boundaries: Unstressed possessives are kt:es-possessives-unstressed; ambiguity of suyo (de él / de ella / de usted) is resolved by context or de + pronoun

primitives.binding: Objects and owners in a scene; learner answers ¿De quién es? and must choose mío/mía/míos by the object
mi / mío placement: learner moves the possessive before or after the noun and the form changes accordingly

kcs.label: Quantifiers and indefinites: todo, alguno, algo, nadie, demasiado
kcs.description: Indefinites refer to unspecified people, things and amounts: alguien / nadie, algo / nada, algún(o)/a / ningún(o)/a, todo/a/os/as (todos los días, todo el mundo), otro/a (without un: otro café), demasiado, bastante, poco/a, mucho/a, varios/as. Ordinals shorten before masculine nouns: primer, tercer. Existence and absence: ¿Hay alguien? No hay nadie.
forms: algún libro / ningún libro; alguna / ninguna
todo el día, toda la semana, todos los días, todo el mundo

examples.es: ¿Tienes algún libro en español? – No, no tengo ninguno.
examples.en: Do you have any books in Spanish? – No, I don't have any.

examples.es: Todos mis amigos quieren otro café, pero ya no queda nada.
examples.en: All my friends want another coffee, but there's nothing left.

mastery: Chooses the positive or negative indefinite in questions and answers
Uses todo with the article and otro without un
Describes what there is and isn't in a fridge or a room
commonErrors: EN: *un otro café
EN: *todos días (todos los días)
EN: *algunos personas (agreement)
EN: *Ningunos libros (plural ninguno is rare)
boundaries: Double negation (No hay nadie) is kt:es-double-negation; muy/mucho is kt:es-muy-mucho

kcs.label: Negation with nunca, nadie, nada, tampoco
kcs.description: Negative words (nada, nadie, nunca, ninguno, tampoco) need no before the verb when they come after it (No veo a nadie. No he comido nada), but not when they come first (Nadie lo sabe. Nunca bebo café). Ni… ni… links negatives. Negative answers are often short: ¿Has visto algo? – No, nada.
forms: no + verb + nada / nadie / nunca / ningún…
negative word first, no "no": Nadie viene. Tampoco yo.
ni… ni…: No tengo ni hermanos ni hermanas.

examples.es: No hay nadie en la oficina y no funciona nada.
examples.en: There's nobody in the office and nothing works.

examples.es: Nunca como carne. – Yo tampoco.
examples.en: I never eat meat. – Me neither.

mastery: Uses no + verb + negative word correctly
Moves the negative word to the front and drops no
Describes what they never do and what nobody in their family does
commonErrors: EN: avoids the "double negative" and uses algo/alguien: *No veo alguien
EN: keeps no with a fronted negative: *Nadie no viene
EN: *No tengo nada hermanos
boundaries: Basic negation and word order are kt:es-negation-word-order; también/tampoco is kt:es-tambien-tampoco

primitives.binding: English "I don't see anyone" vs No veo a nadie: learner aligns words and notes Spanish needs a negative word in both places
Learner moves nadie / nunca to the front and back of the sentence and adds or removes no

kcs.label: When to use an article and when not
kcs.description: Definite article with generalisations (Me gusta el café; Los perros son fieles), days for "on" (el lunes), percentages and body parts. Indefinite article for introducing something new, but not with professions after ser (Es médica), not with otro, medio, ¿qué…? (¡Qué casa!). No article with uncountable or plural nouns for unspecified amounts (Bebo agua; Escribo cartas), with tener + typical possessions (Tiene coche; Tiene perro), and after hay with a plural or uncountable (Hay tomates).
forms: generalising: Los niños necesitan dormir. Me encanta el chocolate.
unspecified quantity, no article: Compro pan y huevos.
ser + profession: Soy profesor (but Es un profesor excelente)
no un with otro / medio / cien / mil
encantar / gustar need a determiner: Me encanta el cine (not *cine)

examples.es: No bebo café, pero me encanta el té.
examples.en: I don't drink coffee, but I love tea.

examples.es: ¿Tienes coche? – No, tengo moto.
examples.en: Do you have a car? – No, I have a motorbike.

mastery: Chooses article, indefinite or zero in a gap-fill
Explains the difference between Bebo leche and Me gusta la leche
Corrects article errors in their own writing
commonErrors: EN: *Me gusta café / *Los niños necesitan dormir is fine but *Niños necesitan dormir is not
EN: *Soy un estudiante (correct only with an adjective)
EN: *un otro / *un medio kilo / *un cien
boundaries: Basic article forms are kt:es-articles; hay vs estar is kt:es-hay-vs-estar

primitives.binding: Learner judges sentences with and without articles against the generalisation / unspecified-amount rules and sorts exceptions
English "I like coffee" vs Me gusta el café: learner aligns and finds where Spanish adds or drops the article

kcs.label: Gender: exceptions and tricky nouns
kcs.description: Beyond -o/-a, some nouns break the pattern: el día, el mapa, el problema, el idioma, el tema, el programa (masculine in -a); la mano, la radio, la foto, la moto (feminine in -o; foto and moto are short for fotografía, motocicleta); nouns in -ista and -nte are often common gender (el/la turista, el/la estudiante). Feminine nouns beginning with stressed a take el in the singular: el agua fría, el aula. Some animals have one gender for both sexes (la jirafa, el caimán).
forms: masculine in -ma: el problema, el tema, el idioma, el programa
el día, el mapa, el sofá
la mano, la foto, la moto, la radio
el/la estudiante, el/la turista, el/la cantante
el agua, el aula, el hambre (feminine: el agua fría)
one-gender animals: la jirafa macho, el caimán hembra (recognition)

examples.es: Tengo un problema: el agua está fría.
examples.en: I have a problem: the water is cold.

examples.es: La foto de la moto está en el mapa.
examples.en: The photo of the motorbike is on the map.

mastery: Assigns gender to 20 tricky nouns
Makes adjectives agree with el agua (fría)
Explains why el agua takes el but is feminine
commonErrors: EN: *la problema, *la día
EN: *el mano
EN: *el agua frío
boundaries: Basic gender rules are kt:es-noun-gender

primitives.binding: Learner tests the -o/-a rule on a list and sorts the counterexamples into groups (-ma, short forms, stressed a)
Spaced recall of article + noun for the exception list

kcs.label: Estar + gerund: actions in progress
kcs.description: Estar + gerund (-ando, -iendo) describes an action in progress at the moment of speaking or around now: Estoy comiendo. Estamos estudiando mucho este mes. Irregular gerunds: leyendo, oyendo, durmiendo, pidiendo, diciendo, yendo. Unlike English, it is not used for plans (Mañana voy a Lima, not *estoy yendo).
forms: leyendo, oyendo, yendo, durmiendo, pidiendo, diciendo
pronouns: Estoy duchándome / Me estoy duchando

examples.es: ¿Qué estás haciendo? – Estoy preparando la cena.
examples.en: What are you doing? – I'm making dinner.

examples.es: Este año estoy aprendiendo a tocar la guitarra.
examples.en: This year I'm learning to play the guitar.

mastery: Forms regular and irregular gerunds
Describes what people in a picture are doing
Explains in a call what everyone at home is doing
commonErrors: EN: uses it for the future: *Estoy viajando a Perú el mes que viene
EN: uses it with ser: *Soy estudiando
EN: *leiendo, *duermiendo
boundaries: Past progressive (estaba + gerund) is recognised in narratives only

primitives.binding: Busy-street scene; learner says what each person is doing; gerund form and estar agreement checked
Now marker on a timeline; learner distinguishes in-progress (estoy comiendo), habit (como) and plan (voy a comer)

kcs.label: Linking events in time: cuando, antes de, después de, desde que, hasta
kcs.description: Cuando + indicative links habitual or past events: Cuando llego a casa, ceno. Cuando era niño, vivía en Lima. Antes de / después de + infinitive when the subject is the same: Antes de salir, cierro la puerta. Desde (que), hasta (que) mark limits. Cuando + future time needs the subjunctive and is B1.
forms: cuando + present (habit): Cuando llueve, me quedo en casa.
cuando + past: Cuando llegué, ya no había nadie.
antes de / después de + infinitive (same subject)
desde + noun / desde que + verb: desde que vivo aquí
hasta + noun / time: hasta el lunes

examples.es: Cuando termino de trabajar, voy al gimnasio.
examples.en: When I finish work, I go to the gym.

examples.es: Después de comer, siempre duermo la siesta.
examples.en: After lunch I always have a nap.

mastery: Joins two events with cuando, antes de or después de
Uses the infinitive after antes de / después de
Describes their routine with time clauses
commonErrors: EN: *Después de comí (infinitive)
EN: *Cuando llegaré mañana (B1 subjunctive; learners use future)
EN: *Antes de que salir
boundaries: Cuando + subjunctive for future events is B1

primitives.binding: Two simple sentences combined with cuando / antes de / después de, and complex sentences unpacked back into two
Two events on a timeline; learner chooses the linking word from their order

kcs.label: How long: desde, desde hace, hace… que, llevar
kcs.description: Duration of a situation that continues now: present + desde hace + period (Vivo aquí desde hace tres años), Hace + period + que + present (Hace tres años que vivo aquí), present + desde + starting point (desde 2020, desde el lunes), llevar + period (+ gerund) (Llevo tres años aquí). Question: ¿Desde cuándo…? ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que…?
forms: llevar + period (+ gerund): Llevo dos años estudiando español.

examples.es: Estudio español desde hace dos años.
examples.en: I've been studying Spanish for two years.

examples.es: ¿Desde cuándo trabajas aquí? – Desde enero.
examples.en: Since when have you worked here? – Since January.

mastery: Chooses desde or desde hace by whether a point or a period follows
Converts between desde hace and hace… que
Tells how long they have done several activities
commonErrors: EN: uses the perfect as in English: *He vivido aquí desde hace tres años (present is normal)
EN: *por tres años for ongoing duration
EN: *desde tres años
boundaries: hace + period for a past point (hace tres años = three years ago) is kt:es-past-time-markers

primitives.binding: Bar from a start point to now; learner labels the start (desde) or the length (desde hace)
English "I have lived here for…" vs Vivo aquí desde hace…: learner aligns tense and preposition

kcs.label: More question words: cuál, cuánto, de quién, para qué
kcs.description: Extends A1 questions: ¿cuál / cuáles? (which one(s), also with ser: ¿Cuál es tu número?) vs ¿qué + noun?; ¿cuánto/a/os/as? with agreement; ¿cuándo?; preposition + interrogative at the start: ¿De dónde…?, ¿Con quién…?, ¿Para qué…?, ¿De quién es…?, ¿A qué hora…?, ¿Por qué…?; asking for information politely: ¿Sabe usted…? ¿Me puede decir…?

examples.en: Which do you prefer, the red one or the green one?

examples.es: ¿Con quién vas a ir y para qué?
examples.en: Who are you going with and what for?

kcs.label: Real conditions: si + present
kcs.description: Si + present + present / future / ir a / imperative expresses real or likely conditions: Si llueve, no salimos. Si tienes tiempo, llámame. Si estudias, vas a aprobar. Si (if) has no accent; sí (yes) does.
forms: si + present, present: Si hace sol, voy a la playa.
si + present, imperative: Si ves a Ana, salúdala.
si + present, ir a / future: Si no comes, vas a tener hambre.
the si clause can go first or second

examples.en: If you like, I'll go with you to the doctor.

examples.es: Si mañana hace buen tiempo, vamos a ir de excursión.

kcs.label: Reasons and consequences: porque, como, por eso, así que
kcs.description: Giving reasons: porque (after the main clause), como (at the start: Como llovía, no salimos), es que (excuse, spoken). Consequences: por eso, así que, entonces. Contrast: pero, sin embargo (written), aunque + indicative (recognition).

examples.es: Como no tenía dinero, no fui a la excursión.

Uses como only at the start of a sentence

EN: *por eso que
EN: *entonces used for "then" in time only
boundaries: ¿Por qué? / porque are kt:es-porque-por-que; sequence connectors are kt:es-sequencing-connectors

kcs.label: Por and para: core uses
kcs.description: Para: purpose (para + infinitive: para aprender), destination (el tren para Madrid), recipient (es para ti), deadline (para el lunes), opinion (para mí). Por: cause (por el tráfico), through/around (por el parque, por aquí), means (por teléfono, por correo), part of day (por la mañana), price/exchange (por diez euros), approximate time/place.
forms: por + cause: Gracias por…, por la lluvia
por + place: through, around: Paseo por el centro.
por + means: por teléfono, por internet

examples.es: Este regalo es para mi madre; lo he comprado por internet.

boundaries: Full por/para contrast (on behalf of, passive agent, duration nuances) is B1
en la mañana is used in parts of Latin America

kcs.label: Agreeing, disagreeing and taking a position
kcs.description: Taking a position (Estoy a favor de / en contra de…), asking whether someone agrees (¿Estás de acuerdo? ¿Verdad? ¿No crees?), agreeing (Estoy de acuerdo, Tienes razón, Claro, Exacto, Yo también / Yo tampoco), partial agreement (Sí, pero…, Depende) and disagreeing (No estoy de acuerdo, No tienes razón, Yo no; softened: Bueno, no sé…).
forms: Estoy a favor de / en contra de + noun / infinitive
Estoy de acuerdo (contigo). / Tienes razón. / Exacto.
No estoy de acuerdo. / Yo no lo veo así.
Yo también / Yo tampoco / Yo sí / Yo no

examples.es: Creo que el centro debería ser peatonal. ¿Estás de acuerdo? – Sí, tienes razón.
examples.en: I think the centre should be pedestrian. Do you agree? – Yes, you're right.

examples.es: Estoy en contra de los deberes los fines de semana. – Bueno, depende.
examples.en: I'm against homework at weekends. – Well, it depends.

mastery: Classifies responses as agreement, partial agreement or disagreement
Responds to five opinions with varied expressions
Takes part in a short discussion with polite disagreement
commonErrors: EN: *Estoy acuerdo / *Soy de acuerdo
EN: *Tengo razón for "you're right" (tienes razón)
EN: disagrees bluntly with No without softening
boundaries: Giving opinions with creo que is kt:es-fn-opinion-creo-que

primitives.binding: Debate cards (school uniforms, cars in the centre); learner responds and the partner pushes back; one response must be partial agreement
Place response expressions on a scale from total agreement to total disagreement

kcs.label: How sure: certainty, probability and doubt
kcs.description: Certainty: Estoy seguro/a de que…, Seguro que…, Claro que…, Sé que…. Uncertainty: No estoy seguro/a, No sé si…, Creo que sí / no, Quizás / Tal vez + indicative (at A2), A lo mejor + indicative, Puede ser. Evidence: Está claro, Es verdad, Es mentira.
forms: No estoy seguro. / No sé si…
A lo mejor + indicative: A lo mejor llueve.
Quizás / Tal vez (+ indicative at A2)
Es verdad. / Es mentira. / Puede ser.

examples.es: ¿Viene Marta? – No estoy segura; a lo mejor viene más tarde.
examples.en: Is Marta coming? – I'm not sure; maybe she'll come later.

examples.es: Estoy seguro de que el museo cierra a las ocho.
examples.en: I'm sure the museum closes at eight.

mastery: Places expressions on a certainty scale
Answers questions with graded certainty
Uses a lo mejor with indicative correctly
commonErrors: EN: *Estoy seguro que (de que is the norm, though "seguro que" is frequent in speech)
EN: *A lo mejor llueva (indicative)
EN: *Maybe for quizás overuses one form
boundaries: Quizás + subjunctive is B1
Possibility (puede que, es posible) at A1 is kt:es-fn-possibility

primitives.binding: Certainty ladder from sé que / estoy seguro to no tengo ni idea; learner places answers to a quiz by confidence
Mystery photos; learner guesses with a lo mejor / seguro que and checks

kcs.label: Remembering and forgetting
kcs.description: Asking and saying whether you remember: ¿Te acuerdas de…? ¿Recuerdas…? Sí, me acuerdo / Sí, lo recuerdo / No me acuerdo / No me acuerdo de su nombre / Se me ha olvidado / He olvidado… Acordarse is reflexive and takes de; recordar takes a direct object.
forms: Sí, me acuerdo. / No me acuerdo.
Me he olvidado de… / He olvidado… / Se me ha olvidado…

examples.es: ¿Te acuerdas de Pedro, el de la universidad? – Sí, claro que me acuerdo.
examples.en: Do you remember Pedro, from university? – Yes, of course I remember.

examples.es: Lo siento, se me ha olvidado tu nombre.
examples.en: Sorry, I've forgotten your name.

mastery: Uses acordarse de and recordar with the right structure
Says politely that they have forgotten something
Talks about shared memories with a partner
commonErrors: EN: *Me acuerdo su nombre (de)
EN: *Recuerdo de… (no de with recordar)
EN: *Yo olvidé de… mixing structures
boundaries: Reflexive verbs in general are kt:es-reflexive-verbs; se me ha olvidado is learned as a chunk

primitives.binding: Acordarse de / recordar / olvidar(se de) in contexts; learner chooses the structure that fits
Reunion with an old classmate: learner asks and answers ¿Te acuerdas de…?, including admitting they have forgotten

kcs.label: Telephone calls and messages
kcs.description: Answering (¿Sí? ¿Diga? ¿Dígame? ¿Aló? ¿Bueno?), asking for someone (¿Está Carmen? ¿Puedo hablar con…?), identifying yourself (Soy Pedro / Hola, soy Pedro), asking for an extension or room (¿Me pone con la extensión 25 / con la habitación 104?), responding (Sí, un momento / No está / Se ha equivocado), and leaving a message (¿Puedo dejarle un recado? ¿Le digo que te llame?). Voicemail and WhatsApp audio follow similar formulas.
forms: Soy… / De parte de… / ¿De parte de quién?
Un momento, por favor. / No está. / Se ha equivocado de número.
¿Quiere dejar un recado? / ¿Le digo que la llame?

examples.es: ¿Diga? – Hola, ¿está Carmen? – No, no está. ¿Quieres dejarle un recado?
examples.en: Hello? – Hi, is Carmen there? – No, she isn't. Do you want to leave her a message?

examples.es: Buenos días, ¿me pone con la habitación 214, por favor?
examples.en: Good morning, could you put me through to room 214, please?

mastery: Follows a recorded phone call and notes who, why and what message
Makes a call asking for someone and leaves a message
Takes a message for someone else and writes it down
commonErrors: EN: *Esto es Pedro / *Es Pedro aquí (Soy Pedro)
EN: *¿Puedo hablar a Carmen? (con)
EN: says Hola only and doesn't identify themselves
boundaries: Phone formulas vary by country; the variety shown is noted on each formula
Getting attention is kt:es-fn-attention-getters

primitives.binding: Calls to a friend's home, a hotel and an office; branches for absent person, wrong number and message-taking
Voicemails: learner extracts caller, reason, number and time to call back

levels.locator: PCIC · Funciones · Inventario A1-A2 · 6.3 · columna A2

kcs.label: Keeping track: reference, ellipsis and avoiding repetition
kcs.description: Spanish keeps track of people and things without repeating them: subject omission (Ana vive en Lima. Trabaja en un banco), object pronouns (Lo vi), demonstratives (eso), possessive pronouns (el mío) and ellipsis in replies (¿Quién viene? – Yo. ¿Vienes? – Sí). Subject pronouns are added for contrast or to resolve ambiguity (Él trabaja y ella estudia).
forms: drop the repeated subject: Tengo un hermano. Se llama Leo.
pronoun for the object: Compré un libro y lo leí.
eso / esto for whole ideas: Eso es verdad.
short answers: – ¿Quién quiere café? – Yo. / Yo no.
add él / ella for contrast or ambiguity

examples.es: Tengo una amiga en Bogotá. Es profesora y la visito cada verano.
examples.en: I have a friend in Bogotá. She's a teacher and I visit her every summer.

examples.es: ¿Quién ha roto esto? – Yo no. – Pues yo tampoco.
examples.en: Who broke this? – Not me. – Well, not me either.

mastery: Rewrites a repetitive text using omission and pronouns
Links pronouns to their referents in a text
Adds a subject pronoun only where contrast or ambiguity requires it
commonErrors: EN: repeats yo / él in every sentence
EN: repeats the full noun instead of a pronoun
ZH: omits object pronouns where Spanish needs them
boundaries: Object pronoun forms are kt:es-direct-object-pronouns and kt:es-indirect-object-pronouns

primitives.binding: Learner draws links from each pronoun or omitted subject back to its referent in a short story
Learner revises a repetitive paragraph, fixing only repetition; the change is compared with the original

kcs.label: Spoken interaction: everyday conversations (A2)
kcs.description: Taking part in short everyday conversations and transactions: chatting about routines, plans, experiences and preferences, making arrangements, dealing with services (bank, post, doctor, hotel, repairs), using interaction strategies (asking for repetition, checking understanding, backchannelling, turn-taking and interrupting politely: Perdona que te interrumpa, pero…).
forms: opening and closing a chat: ¿Qué tal todo? / Bueno, te dejo.
closing: Venga, hasta luego. / Nos vemos.

examples.es: Bueno, te dejo, que tengo que irme. ¡Nos vemos el sábado!
examples.en: Well, I'll let you go, I have to be off. See you on Saturday!

examples.es: Perdona que te interrumpa, pero ¿a qué hora empieza?
examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but what time does it start?

mastery: Sustains a 3–4 minute conversation on a familiar topic
Opens and closes a conversation naturally
Completes a service transaction with an unexpected complication
commonErrors: EN: answers with single words and does not return questions
EN: ends abruptly without a closing formula
EN: interrupts without a softener
boundaries: Long discussions and negotiations are B1

primitives.binding: Branching café chat and service encounters; each branch requires a turn-taking or repair move
Learner practises interrupting, checking and closing formulas in a fast-paced dialogue
Learner records a role play, transcribes it and marks where they missed a turn or closing

kcs.label: Listening: announcements, conversations and short broadcasts (A2)
kcs.description: Understanding the main point of short, clear, slow recorded or live speech on familiar topics: public announcements (station, airport, shop), simple instructions, everyday conversations between native speakers, weather forecasts, short news items and advertisements. Includes perception of what is heard and seen (oír vs escuchar, ver vs mirar).
forms: announcements: El tren con destino a… efectuará su salida por la vía 3.
forecasts and ads: key numbers, places, times
listening strategies: predict, listen for key words, check

examples.es: Atención: el vuelo IB3456 con destino a Buenos Aires sale por la puerta 12.
examples.en: Attention: flight IB3456 to Buenos Aires departs from gate 12.

examples.es: ¿Oyes eso? – Sí, escucha: es la canción que te dije.
examples.en: Can you hear that? – Yes, listen: it's the song I told you about.

mastery: Extracts gate, time and destination from an announcement
Identifies the topic and outcome of a short conversation
Distinguishes oír / escuchar and ver / mirar
commonErrors: EN: tries to understand every word and loses the main point
EN: *escuchar un ruido (oír)
EN: *ver la tele vs mirar is fine but *mirar una película in cinema is less common
boundaries: A1 listening is kt:es-act-listening-a1; fast or accented speech is B1+

primitives.binding: Station and airport announcements; learner fills a departure board
Learner predicts the next line or decision in a conversation before hearing it
After listening, learner compares their notes with the transcript and marks what they missed

kcs.label: Welcoming, congratulating and good wishes
kcs.description: Welcoming (¡Bienvenido/a/os/as! Pasa, pasa; estás en tu casa), responding (Gracias, qué casa tan bonita), congratulating (¡Felicidades! ¡Enhorabuena! ¡Feliz cumpleaños! ¡Feliz Navidad! ¡Felices fiestas!), good wishes (¡Que te mejores! ¡Que tengas buen viaje! ¡Buen fin de semana! ¡Que aproveche! ¡Suerte!) and responding (Gracias, igualmente; Muchas gracias, tú también). Festivals and celebrations vary by country.
forms: ¡Que te mejores! / ¡Que lo pases bien! / ¡Que tengas suerte! (fixed chunks)

examples.es: ¡Enhorabuena por el nuevo trabajo! – Muchas gracias.
examples.en: Congratulations on the new job! – Thank you very much.

examples.es: Me voy de vacaciones mañana. – ¡Que lo pases muy bien! – Gracias, igualmente.
examples.en: I'm going on holiday tomorrow. – Have a great time! – Thanks, you too.

mastery: Matches occasions with the right wish or congratulation
Responds to wishes with igualmente / gracias
Writes a short card for a birthday, a wedding or a recovery
commonErrors: EN: *¡Felicitaciones! is used in Latin America; ¡Enhorabuena! is common in Spain — learners mix them freely, which is fine
EN: *¡Ten un buen día! calqued (¡Que tengas un buen día! / ¡Buen día!)
EN: uses ¡Feliz cumpleaños! for any celebration
boundaries: ¡Que + subjunctive! wishes are learned as chunks; productive present subjunctive is B1
Specific festivals (Día de Muertos, Reyes, Semana Santa, fiestas patrias) are examples, not a fixed list

primitives.binding: Guest arrives, someone sneezes, a colleague gets a promotion: learner chooses the expected formula; a mismatched choice shows the reaction
Card templates for birthday, wedding, get well; learner fills in and then writes one without a template

kcs.label: Writing short letters, emails and messages (A2)
kcs.description: Writing short personal letters and emails (thanks, apology, invitation, news) and simple formal messages (request for information, booking): openings (Querida Ana; Hola, ¿qué tal?; Estimado/a señor/a:), body with connectors, closings (Un abrazo, Besos, Un saludo, Atentamente), and form conventions (colon after formal opening, date format).
forms: formal: Estimado/a señor/a: / Le escribo para…
body: Te escribo para… / Gracias por… / Siento no…
closing: Un abrazo / Besos / Un saludo / Atentamente
P. D.; date: Madrid, 3 de mayo de 2026

examples.es: Querida Lucía: ¿Qué tal? Te escribo para contarte que el mes que viene voy a Valencia. Un abrazo, Tom.
examples.en: Dear Lucía, How are you? I'm writing to tell you that next month I'm going to Valencia. Love, Tom.

examples.es: Estimados señores: Les escribo para pedir información sobre los cursos de verano. Atentamente, …
examples.en: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to request information about the summer courses. Yours faithfully, …

mastery: Chooses opening and closing to fit the reader
Writes an 80–100 word informal email giving news and making a plan
Writes a short formal request for information
commonErrors: EN: *Querido señor (formal: Estimado señor)
EN: comma after formal opening (Spanish uses a colon)
EN: *Sinceramente as a closing (Atentamente / Un saludo)
boundaries: Short messages at A1 are kt:es-act-short-messages; formal correspondence beyond simple requests is B1

primitives.binding: Email skeletons for informal news and formal request; learner fills slots, then removes the scaffold for a second email
Same content to a friend and to a language school; learner adjusts opening, pronouns and closing
Feedback on one aspect only (register), learner revises and compares

kcs.description: Reading short, simple texts on familiar topics: personal letters and emails, ads, menus, timetables, leaflets, short news, instructions, simple stories and web pages. examples.en: Central flat to let, 2 bedrooms, furnished. €750/month. Call in the afternoons.

kcs.label: Describing people, objects and places in texts (A2)
kcs.description: Producing short descriptive texts: a person (appearance, character, what they do, their relationship to you), an object (form, material, use) and a place (location, what there is, atmosphere, comparison with others). Combines ser/estar, hay, comparatives, adjective agreement and connectors.
forms: person: Es…, Tiene…, Lleva…, Siempre está…
object: Es de…, Sirve para…, Es más… que…
place: Está en…, Hay…, Es un sitio…
connectors: además, también, pero, sobre todo

examples.es: Mi pueblo está en la montaña. Es pequeño y tranquilo, y tiene una plaza muy bonita.
examples.en: My village is in the mountains. It's small and quiet, and it has a very pretty square.

examples.es: Mi abuela es bajita y lleva gafas. Es muy divertida y siempre está contenta.
examples.en: My grandmother is short and wears glasses. She's great fun and is always happy.

mastery: Writes a 60–80 word description of a person and one of a place
Orders a description from general to specific
Describes their hometown orally for one minute
commonErrors: EN: lists facts without connectors
EN: mixes ser and estar in place descriptions (*El pueblo es en la montaña)
EN: agreement errors in long noun phrases
boundaries: Short A1 descriptions are kt:es-act-describe-a1

primitives.binding: Learner starts with three facts about a place, then adds location, comparison, atmosphere and opinion
Photo of a place; learner describes it for someone who can't see it; listener checks key features
Learner writes first, compares with a model description, and notes one technique to borrow

kcs.label: Basic mediation: relaying information across languages and cultures
kcs.description: Passing on simple information to someone who does not understand Spanish (or vice versa): relaying a sign, an announcement, a menu item or a short message in the other language; explaining a simple cultural difference to a visitor (meal times, greetings, tú/usted); asking for clarification on someone's behalf.
forms: Dice que… / Pone que… (the sign says…)
Mi amigo no habla español; ¿puede repetir?
In English: "She says the train is late."
explaining customs: Aquí se cena más tarde.

examples.es: Mi amiga no habla español. Pregunta si hay platos sin gluten.
examples.en: My friend doesn't speak Spanish. She's asking if there are gluten-free dishes.

examples.es: El cartel pone que el museo está cerrado los lunes.
examples.en: The sign says the museum is closed on Mondays.

mastery: Relays the key point of a Spanish sign or announcement in English
Asks a Spanish speaker questions on behalf of a non-speaker
Explains a cultural difference to a visitor in simple terms
commonErrors: EN: translates word by word instead of relaying the point
EN: *Ella dice que el tren es tarde (llega tarde)
boundaries: Reported speech with tense changes is B1; here dice que / pregunta si + present only

primitives.binding: Three-way scene: tourist (English), learner, waiter (Spanish); learner relays questions and answers
Learner aligns a Spanish notice with their English relay and checks no key information was lost

citations.locator: CEFR Companion Volume 2020 · mediation (not obtained this round)

kcs.label: Noticing and reflecting on cultural differences
kcs.description: Becoming aware of cultural practices in Spanish-speaking societies and comparing them with one's own without stereotyping: traditions and social change, diversity of religions and beliefs, immigration and multicultural communities, festivals; noticing one's reactions, asking respectful questions, and adapting behaviour. Spanish-speaking countries differ widely; generalisations should be tested.
forms: noticing: Aquí la gente… / En mi país…
asking: ¿Es normal aquí…? ¿Cómo se hace en…?
comparing: En mi país también / En cambio, en mi país…
avoiding stereotypes: Depende de la región / de la persona.
reflecting: Me sorprendió que… (chunk) / Me pareció raro…

examples.es: En mi país cenamos a las seis; aquí mucha gente cena a las nueve o más tarde.
examples.en: In my country we have dinner at six; here a lot of people have dinner at nine or later.

examples.es: ¿Es normal dar dos besos cuando conoces a alguien? – Depende del país y de la situación.
examples.en: Is it normal to give two kisses when you meet someone? – It depends on the country and the situation.

mastery: Describes a cultural difference they have noticed without generalising to all Spanish speakers
Asks a respectful question about a custom
Compares a festival in a Spanish-speaking country with one from their own culture
commonErrors: EN: generalises Spain to all Spanish-speaking countries
EN: presents customs as exotic or as fixed national traits
boundaries: PCIC Habilidades y actitudes are not graded by level; this KC takes the first steps (noticing, comparing, asking)
Factual cultural content is in kt:es-cult-society-arts and kt:es-soc-greeting-customs

primitives.binding: Incidents (dinner time, personal space, punctuality) with several interpretations; learner chooses and justifies, then sees variation by country
Same custom across several countries; learner notes differences and avoids a single "Spanish" answer

abrir una cuenta / cambiar euros a pesos
enviar una carta / un paquete; correos
la comisaría / denunciar un robo / perder la cartera

kcs.label: Society, history and the arts: first references
kcs.description: A first set of widely known cultural references from the Spanish-speaking world: political organisation in simple terms (el gobierno, el presidente, el rey, las elecciones), religion and beliefs (diversity, main festivals), key historical figures and events, and the arts (writers, painters, musicians, films, architecture). Learners talk about what they know and like, using past tenses for biography.
forms: el gobierno, el presidente / la presidenta, el rey, las elecciones, votar
la religión, la iglesia, la mezquita, la sinagoga; festivals
artes: la pintura, la música, el cine, la arquitectura, la literatura
biography: nació en…, fue…, escribió / pintó…

examples.es: Gabriela Mistral fue una poeta chilena y ganó el Premio Nobel en 1945.
examples.en: Gabriela Mistral was a Chilean poet and won the Nobel Prize in 1945.

examples.es: Me gusta mucho la música de Rosalía y el cine de Guillermo del Toro.
examples.en: I really like Rosalía's music and Guillermo del Toro's films.

mastery: Names a cultural figure from three different countries and what they did
Presents a work of art or a building in a few sentences
Talks about the political system of a Spanish-speaking country in simple terms
commonErrors: EN: assumes all references are from Spain
EN: *el presidente de España (Spain has a presidente del Gobierno and a king)
boundaries: PCIC Referentes culturales lists references per country and phase; here examples are illustrative and should be chosen with the learner's target region
Politics and religion are sensitive; the KC covers vocabulary and factual description only

primitives.binding: Short museum and concert listings; learner finds who, what, where
Picture timeline of an artist's life; learner retells it in the preterite
Learner meets references from several countries and decides which country each belongs to
